title: Final Capstone: Your Own Project
body: Pick something you care about and build it properly. Ideas: - A multiplayer game with an Asio server - A ray tracer (multi-threaded, BVH acceleration, PPM/PNG output) - A database engine (B-tree storage, SQL-subset parser, transactions) - A text editor (gap buffer/rope, syntax highlighting, undo tree) - An emulator (CHIP-8 → Game Boy) - A compiler for a small language to LLVM IR or x86 assembly Requirements:

title: Common errors explained
body: !tip Golden rule Fix the first error, rebuild, repeat. Later errors are often side-effects of the first. Compiler errors Message (GCC / MSVC wording varies) Usually means Fix --- --- --- expected ';' before ... missing semicolon on the previous line add ; 'x' was not declared in this scope / undeclared identifier typo, missing include , wrong scope, used before declared check spelling/scope; add header or forward declaration 'cout' is not a member of 'std' missing include <iostream include the header no matching function for call to ... wrong argument types/count read the "candidates" list below it call of overloaded 'f(...)' is ambiguous two overloads equally good cast an argument or add an exact overload ( 4.01 Overloading and Default Arguments ) narrowing conversion of ... from 'double' to 'int' brace-init lost precision use static_cast ( 2.05 Type Conversion and static_cast ) assignment of read-only variable modifying a const remove const or don't modify passing 'const X' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers calling a non-const member function on a const object mark the member function const ( 6.04 this and const Member Functions ) cannot bind non-const lvalue reference ... to an rvalue passing a temporary to T& take const T& or T&& use of deleted function copying a non-copyable type ( unique_ptr , jthread , stream) std::move it or pass by reference invalid use of incomplete type only forward-declared where full definition needed include the header ( 6.06 Class Files and Nested Types ) cannot declare variable 'x' to be of abstract type a pure virtual function isn't overridden implement it ( 8.05 Abstract Classes and Interfaces ) 'override' ... does not override signature mismatch (const? param type?) match the base exactly jump to case label crosses initialization variable defined inside a case wrap the case body in { } ( 3.02 switch ) template argument deduction/substitution failed T couldn't be deduced / conflicting specify f<double (...) ( 4.02 Function Templates ) constraints not satisfied type doesn't meet a concept read which requirement failed ( 9.04 Concepts ) redefinition of ... defined twice (missing header guard, definition in header) pragma once ; move definitions to .cpp ( 1.08 Multiple Files and Headers ) Linker errors Message Means Fix --- --- --- undefined reference to 'foo()' / LNK2019 unresolved external symbol declared but never defined, or the .cpp isn't compiled/linked add the definition / add file to build / link the library multiple definition of 'x' / LNK2005 already defined a non-inline definition in a header included by several .cpp s inline , or move to a .cpp ( 3.06 Global Variables and Linkage ) undefined reference to 'main' / LNK1561 entry point must be defined no main or misspelled write int main() undefined reference to vtable for X a virtual function declared but not defined define all virtuals (often the destructor) cannot open file 'xyz.lib' library path wrong fix library directories ( 10.09 CMake and Libraries ) Runtime crashes Symptom Likely cause Lesson --- --- --- Segmentation fault / Access violation reading 0x00000000 null pointer dereference 4.04 Pointers Access violation at random address dangling pointer, out-of-bounds, use-after-free 7.02 new and delete vector subscript out of range (MSVC debug) bad index 5.01 Vectors std::out_of_range / terminate called after throwing uncaught exception 9.05 Exceptions Stack overflow infinite/deep recursion, huge local arrays 5.09 Recursion · 7.01 Stack vs Heap double free or corruption / heap corruption deleting twice, shallow copy of owning pointer 7.03 Copy Semantics Program hangs infinite loop, deadlock 3.03 Loops · 12.02 Mutexes and Locks Garbage numbers uninitialized variable 1.04 Variables and Initialization Works in Debug, breaks in Release undefined behavior 13.01 Undefined Behavior and Object Lifetime Input loop goes crazy after typing letters cin fail state not cleared 3.07 Input Validation and assert Logic bugs that compile fine - if (x = 5) instead of == - 5 / 2 is 2 (integer division) - for (...); or if (...); stray semicolon - off-by-one: i <= v.size() - unsigned counting down past 0 - comparing floats with == - forgetting break in switch - std::string_view / reference to a temporary that died - object slicing when storing derived objects by value ( 8.06 Slicing, Casting and Composition ) - missing virtual destructor in a polymorphic base !info Turn on -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Wshadow (or /W4 ) and the sanitizers — they catch most of these automatically. See 13.09 Testing, Sanitizers and Static Analysis .

title: 1.01  C# and .NET: Your First Program
body: What C and .NET are, how a program is compiled and run, the dotnet command-line tool, top-level statements, Console.WriteLine and ReadLine, comments, and reading compiler errors. C and .NET C is a statically typed language from Microsoft, used for desktop and web applications, cloud services, tools and games (Unity and Godot use it). .NET is the platform it runs on: a runtime that executes the program, manages memory with a garbage collector, and a large standard library for text, collections, files, networking and much more. .NET is free, open source and runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Compiling turns C into IL (intermediate language) stored in a .dll . When the program starts, the runtime compiles the IL to machine code for the processor it runs on (just-in-time compilation). You get the safety of a managed language with speed close to C++. Your first program csharp // Program.cs Console.WriteLine("Hello, Xenon!"); Console.WriteLine(2 + 3); This is a complete program. Code written at the top of Program.cs , outside any class, is made of top-level statements : the compiler wraps it in a Main method for you. Each statement ends with a semicolon. Console.WriteLine prints a line; Console.Write prints without moving to a new line. Reading input csharp Console.Write("What is your name? "); string? name = Console.ReadLine(); Console.WriteLine($"Hello, {name}!"); Console.Write("Your age? "); int age = int.Parse(Console.ReadLine()!); Console.WriteLine($"Next year you will be {age + 1}."); Console.ReadLine() returns the line typed, or null when the input has ended, so its type is string? (a string that may be null; lesson 2.05). int.Parse turns text into a whole number. The $"..." string can include values in braces: an interpolated string (lesson 1.04). The Run button on examples like this one asks for input below the output. Comments csharp // A comment to the end of the line. / A comment that can span lines. / /// <summary An XML documentation comment, shown by editors when you hover.</summary Console.WriteLine("Comments are ignored by the compiler."); The dotnet tool On your own computer, install the .NET SDK from dot.net. The dotnet command creates, builds and runs projects: bash dotnet new console -o Hello a new console project in the folder Hello cd Hello dotnet run compile and run dotnet build compile only A project is a folder with a .csproj file (the project's settings) and .cs source files. Visual Studio, VS Code with the C Dev Kit, and JetBrains Rider all work with these projects. In this course, the practice editor compiles and runs your code on .NET 9 for you. Compiler errors C checks your program before it runs. An error names the file, line and column, a code, and what is wrong: text Program.cs(3,9): error CS0029: Cannot implicitly convert type 'string' to 'int' Program.cs(5,1): error CS1002: ; expected Read the first error first: later ones are often caused by it. The CS number can be searched for in Microsoft's documentation. Warnings (such as an unused variable) do not stop the build, but they usually point at real problems.

title: Input and output
body: Write a program that asks for a name and a birth year, then greets the person and says how old they turn in 2026: Name? Ada Birth year? 1990 Hello, Ada! In 2026 you turn 36. The prompts are written with Console.Write (no new line); the input after them comes from the person typing. Use int.Parse for the year.

title: 1.02  Variables and Types
body: Declaring variables with explicit types and var, the built-in value types - int, long, double, decimal, bool, char - and string, constants, default values, value versus reference types, and converting between types with casts, Parse, TryParse and Convert. Declaring variables Every variable in C has a type that never changes: csharp int count = 3; double price = 2.50; string name = "Ada"; bool done = false; char grade = 'A'; // a single character, in single quotes var total = count price; // var: the compiler infers the type (double here) const int MaxPlayers = 4; // a constant: fixed at compile time count = count + 1; // fine // count = "four"; // error CS0029: cannot convert string to int Console.WriteLine($"{name}: {count} x {price} = {total}, max {MaxPlayers}, grade {grade}, done {done}"); var is still statically typed: var total is a double , decided once. Use var when the type is obvious from the right-hand side ( var list = new List<int () ), and the explicit type when it helps the reader. Names use camelCase for local variables and PascalCase for constants, methods, classes and properties. Number types Type Holds Example --- --- --- int Whole numbers, about ±2.1 billion 42 long Whole numbers, about ±9.2 × 10¹⁸ 42L double Floating point, about 15 digits 3.14 float Floating point, about 7 digits 3.14f decimal Exact decimal, 28 digits: money 19.99m byte 0 to 255 (byte)200 csharp Console.WriteLine(0.1 + 0.2); // 0.30000000000000004: binary floating point Console.WriteLine(0.1m + 0.2m); // 0.3: decimal is exact for decimal fractions Console.WriteLine(int.MaxValue); int big = int.MaxValue; big = big + 1; // wraps around silently Console.WriteLine(big); Console.WriteLine(1_000_000); // underscores make long numbers readable Use int for counts, double for measurements and science, and decimal for money. checked { ... } turns silent overflow into an OverflowException . Value types and reference types Numbers, bool , char and structs (lesson 3.02) are value types : the variable holds the value itself, and assigning copies it. Strings, arrays, lists and classes are reference types : the variable holds a reference to an object, and assigning copies the reference, so both variables see the same object. csharp int a = 1; int b = a; // a copy b = 2; Console.WriteLine(a); // 1 int x = { 1, 2, 3 }; int y = x; // the same array y 0 = 99; Console.WriteLine(x 0 ); // 99 string is a reference type that behaves like a value: strings can never be changed (they are immutable ), so sharing them is safe. Converting csharp int whole = (int)3.99; // explicit cast: cuts off to 3 double d = 7; // int to double is automatic (no information lost) long l = 5; // int to long too int parsed = int.Parse("123"); // text to number; throws FormatException for "12x" bool ok = int.TryParse("12x", out int value); // false, value is 0: no exception double rate = double.Parse("2.5", System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); string text = 42.ToString(); Console.WriteLine($"{whole} {d} {l} {parsed} {ok} {value} {rate} {text}"); Conversions that may lose information need a cast (type) . For user input, prefer TryParse : it returns false instead of throwing. Parsing decimals depends on the computer's culture ( 2.5 or 2,5 ), so pass CultureInfo.InvariantCulture when reading data files. Default values Fields and array elements start with default values : 0 for numbers, false , '\0' , and null for reference types. Local variables have no default: using one before assigning it is error CS0165.

title: Types and conversions
body: Complete the static methods in Solution : csharp public static double ToCelsius(double fahrenheit) // (F - 32) 5 / 9 public static double Average(int a, int b, int c) // the exact average: Average(1, 2, 2) is 1.666... public static int ParseOrDefault(string text, int fallback) // the number in text, or fallback if it is not a whole number public static decimal TotalPrice(decimal unitPrice, int quantity, decimal taxRate) TotalPrice is unitPrice quantity , plus tax at taxRate (0.2 means 20 %), rounded to 2 decimals with halves rounded away from zero .

title: 1.03  Operators and Math
body: Arithmetic and integer division, remainder, compound assignment and increment, comparison and logical operators with short-circuiting, the conditional operator, operator precedence, and the Math class for rounding, powers and roots. Arithmetic csharp int a = 17, b = 5; Console.WriteLine(a + b); // 22 Console.WriteLine(a - b); // 12 Console.WriteLine(a b); // 85 Console.WriteLine(a / b); // 3: int / int cuts off the fraction Console.WriteLine(a % b); // 2: the remainder Console.WriteLine(a / 5.0); // 3.4: one double operand makes it a double division Console.WriteLine((double)a / b); Console.WriteLine(-17 / 5); // -3: rounds toward zero Console.WriteLine(-17 % 5); // -2: the remainder has the sign of the left side Integer division and % are useful together: minutes / 60 hours and minutes % 60 left over. Dividing an int by zero throws DivideByZeroException ; dividing a double by zero gives Infinity or NaN . Assignment shortcuts csharp int score = 10; score += 5; // score = score + 5 score = 2; // 30 score -= 1; // 29 score++; // 30 score--; // 29 Console.WriteLine(score); int i = 5; Console.WriteLine(i++); // prints 5, then i becomes 6 Console.WriteLine(++i); // i becomes 7, then prints 7 Use ++ and -- as statements on their own line; inside larger expressions they are easy to misread. Comparison and logic Operator Meaning --- --- == , != Equal, not equal < , <= , , = Ordering && And: true when both are true \ \ Or: true when either is true ! Not csharp int age = 20; bool hasTicket = true; bool canEnter = age = 18 && hasTicket; bool discount = age < 12 age = 65; Console.WriteLine($"{canEnter} {discount} {!canEnter}"); string? name = null; if (name != null && name.Length 3) Console.WriteLine("long name"); // safe: && stops early && and short-circuit : if the left side already decides the result, the right side is not evaluated. That is what makes the name != null && name.Length 3 check safe. Conditions must be bool : if (count) is an error in C , unlike C or JavaScript. Write if (count != 0) . The conditional operator csharp int n = 7; string parity = n % 2 == 0 ? "even" : "odd"; Console.WriteLine($"{n} is {parity}"); Precedence , / and % bind tighter than + and - ; comparisons come next; then && , then , then ?: , then assignment. When in doubt, add parentheses: (a + b) c . Math csharp Console.WriteLine(Math.Sqrt(16)); // 4 Console.WriteLine(Math.Pow(2, 10)); // 1024 Console.WriteLine(Math.Abs(-3.5)); // 3.5 Console.WriteLine(Math.Max(3, 9)); // 9 Console.WriteLine(Math.Round(2.5)); // 2: rounds halves to even by default Console.WriteLine(Math.Round(2.5, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)); // 3 Console.WriteLine(Math.Round(3.14159, 2)); // 3.14 Console.WriteLine(Math.Floor(-2.5) + " " + Math.Ceiling(2.1)); // -3 3 Console.WriteLine(Math.Clamp(15, 0, 10)); // 10 Console.WriteLine(Math.PI); Math.Round uses banker's rounding (halves go to the even neighbour) unless you ask for MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero , which is the rounding taught in school and usually wanted for money.

title: Operators
body: Complete the methods: csharp public static bool IsLeapYear(int year) // divisible by 4, except centuries, except every 400 years public static string Clock(int minutes) // minutes after midnight as "h:mm": 125 is "2:05" public static int Change(int cents, int coin) // how many coins of that size fit into cents public static bool CanVote(int age, bool isCitizen, bool isRegistered) - Clock wraps around the day: 1440 minutes is "0:00" again, and negative minutes count back from midnight ( -30 is "23:30" ). - CanVote is true for citizens aged 18 or over who are registered.

title: 1.04  Strings and Formatting
body:
Working with text - string literals, escapes, verbatim and raw strings, interpolation with format specifiers and alignment, the common string methods, comparing strings, characters, and building text efficiently with StringBuilder. String literals csharp string plain = "Tab:	Quote:" Backslash:\ Newline:
next line"; string path = @"C:\Users\Ada
otes.txt"; // verbatim: backslashes are literal string json = """ { "name": "Ada", "tags": "math" } """; // raw string: no escaping at all Console.WriteLine(plain); Console.WriteLine(path); Console.WriteLine(json); Raw strings (three or more quotes) keep everything exactly, which suits JSON, SQL and regular expressions. The indentation of the closing quotes is removed from every line. Interpolation and formatting csharp string name = "Ada"; decimal price = 1234.5m; double ratio = 0.4567; int n = 42; Console.WriteLine($"{name} paid {price:C2}"); // currency, depends on the machine's culture Console.WriteLine($"{price:N2}"); // 1,234.50 Console.WriteLine($"{price:F1}"); // 1234.5 Console.WriteLine($"{ratio:P1}"); // 45.7 % Console.WriteLine($"{n:D5} {n:X}"); // 00042 2A Console.WriteLine($" {name,8} {name,-8} "); // right- and left-aligned in 8 characters Console.WriteLine($" {price,10:F2} "); // alignment and format together Console.WriteLine($"{(n 40 ? "big" : "small")}"); // expressions in parentheses After the value, ,width aligns (negative means left) and :format formats. Common formats: F2 fixed decimals, N2 with thousands separators, P percent, D5 zero-padded integer, X hexadecimal, C currency. For dates: {DateTime.Now:yyyy-MM-dd} . N , C and dates follow the computer's culture . Output meant for files or other programs should use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture : price.ToString("F2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) . String methods Strings never change: each method returns a new string. Code Gives --- --- s.Length , s 0 , s ^1 Length, first character, last character s.Substring(start, length) , s 2..5 Part of the string s.ToUpper() , s.ToLower() , s.Trim() Case, without surrounding spaces s.Contains(x) , s.StartsWith(x) , s.EndsWith(x) Tests s.IndexOf(x) , s.LastIndexOf(x) Position, or -1 s.Replace(a, b) , s.Insert(i, x) , s.Remove(i, n) New strings with changes s.Split(',') , string.Join(", ", parts) Split into an array, join back s.PadLeft(5, '0') , s.PadRight(10) Padded string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(s) Null, empty or only spaces csharp string line = " Ada Lovelace, 1815 , mathematician "; string parts = line.Split(',', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries); Console.WriteLine(parts 0 .ToUpper()); Console.WriteLine(int.Parse(parts 1 ) + 200); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", parts)); Console.WriteLine("banana".Replace("an", "AN") + " " + "banana".IndexOf('n') + " " + "banana" 1..4 ); 1..4 is a range : from index 1 up to, not including, 4. ^1 counts from the end. Comparing == compares string contents. For case-insensitive comparison, use string.Equals(a, b, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ; for sorting, string.Compare(a, b, StringComparison.Ordinal) . Characters csharp char c = 'b'; Console.WriteLine(char.IsLetter(c) + " " + char.IsDigit('7') + " " + char.ToUpper(c)); Console.WriteLine((int)c); // 98: its character code Console.WriteLine((char)(c + 1)); // 'c' foreach (char ch in "hi!") Console.Write($" {ch} "); Console.WriteLine(); Building strings Because strings are immutable, += in a loop copies the whole string each time. For many pieces, use a StringBuilder : csharp using System.Text; var sb = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) sb.Append(i).Append(i < 5 ? ", " : "
"); sb.AppendLine("done"); Console.Write(sb.ToString());

title: Working with strings
body: Complete the methods: csharp public static string Initials(string fullName) // "ada king lovelace" gives "A.K.L." public static string Slug(string title) // " Hello, World! C 13 " gives "hello-world-c-13" public static string PriceLine(string item, decimal price) // item left in 12 characters, price right in 8 with 2 decimals public static int CountVowels(string text) // a, e, i, o, u in either case - Initials ignores extra spaces between and around the names. - Slug keeps letters and digits in lower case, turns every run of other characters into one - , and has no - at either end. - PriceLine("Tea", 2.5m) is "Tea 2.50" : 12 characters for the item, then 8 for the price. Write the price with a . whatever the computer's culture: price.ToString("F2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) .

title: 1.05  Control Flow
body: Making decisions with if, else if and else, the switch statement and switch expressions, loops with while, do-while, for and foreach, break and continue, nested loops, and input loops that keep asking until the input is valid. if and else csharp int temperature = 23; if (temperature = 30) { Console.WriteLine("Hot"); } else if (temperature = 18) { Console.WriteLine("Pleasant"); } else { Console.WriteLine("Cold"); } Braces can be left out around a single statement, but always writing them avoids the classic bug where a second indented line is not actually part of the if . switch A switch statement compares one value against cases: csharp string command = "stop"; switch (command) { case "go": case "start": Console.WriteLine("Starting"); break; case "stop": Console.WriteLine("Stopping"); break; default: Console.WriteLine("Unknown command"); break; } Each case ends with break (or return ); C does not let one case fall through into the next by accident. A switch expression produces a value, which is usually neater: csharp int day = 6; string kind = day switch { 6 or 7 = "weekend", = 1 and <= 5 = "weekday", _ = "not a day", }; Console.WriteLine(kind); _ matches anything. Patterns like or , and and = 1 are covered fully in lesson 2.05. while and do-while csharp int n = 27, steps = 0; while (n != 1) { n = n % 2 == 0 ? n / 2 : 3 n + 1; steps++; } Console.WriteLine($"{steps} steps"); do { ... } while (condition); runs the body at least once, which suits "ask, then check": csharp int guess; do { Console.Write("Pick 1 to 3: "); string? line = Console.ReadLine(); if (line == null) break; // the input has ended if (!int.TryParse(line, out guess)) guess = 0; } while (guess < 1 guess 3); for and foreach csharp for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { Console.Write($"{i} "); } Console.WriteLine(); for (int i = 10; i 0; i -= 3) Console.Write($"{i} "); Console.WriteLine(); string names = { "Ada", "Grace", "Linus" }; foreach (string name in names) { Console.WriteLine(name.ToUpper()); } Use for when you need the index or a count, and foreach to visit every item of an array, list, string or any other collection. break and continue csharp int numbers = { 4, 7, -1, 12, 0, 9 }; int sum = 0; foreach (int x in numbers) { if (x < 0) continue; // skip this one if (x == 0) break; // stop the loop sum += x; } Console.WriteLine(sum); // 4 + 7 + 12 = 23 Nested loops csharp for (int row = 1; row <= 3; row++) { for (int col = 1; col <= 4; col++) { Console.Write($"{row col,4}"); } Console.WriteLine(); } break leaves only the innermost loop. To leave several, move the loops into a method and return (lesson 2.01).

title: Number statistics
body: Write a program that reads numbers, one per line, until a line says done (or the input ends), then prints statistics: Number? 4 Number? 10 Number? abc Not a number: abc Number? 7 Number? done Count: 3 Sum: 21 Min: 4 Max: 10 Average: 7.00 - The prompt Number? is written before each line is read. - A line that is not a whole number prints Not a number: <line and is skipped. Spaces around a number are fine. - When no numbers were entered, print just No numbers. - The average has 2 decimals ( F2 ).

title: A bank account at the console
match: A bank account at the console
body: Write a program that keeps one bank account and follows commands typed one per line: deposit 100 Deposited 100.00. Balance: 100.00 withdraw 30.5 Withdrew 30.50. Balance: 69.50 withdraw 500 Not enough money. Balance: 69.50 interest 2 Added interest 1.39. Balance: 70.89 history 1. deposit 100.00 2. withdraw 30.50 3. interest 1.39 quit Goodbye. Final balance: 70.89 Rules: - Write the prompt before reading each line. Commands are not case-sensitive, and extra spaces are ignored. - Amounts are decimal numbers read with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture (so 30.5 works everywhere), rounded to cents as they are read (halves away from zero), and printed with 2 decimals ( F2 , invariant). - deposit <amount and withdraw <amount : the amount must be a number above 0, else print Amount must be a positive number. A withdrawal larger than the balance prints Not enough money. Balance: <balance and changes nothing. - interest <percent : adds balance × percent / 100, rounded to cents with halves away from zero. The percent must be 0 or more (else Amount must be a positive number. ); an interest of 0.00 is still recorded. - balance prints Balance: <balance . - history prints the successful transactions numbered from 1, as in the example, or No transactions. - quit , or the end of the input, prints Goodbye. Final balance: <balance and stops. - Anything else prints Unknown command: <first word , and a command with a missing or extra argument prints Usage: <command <amount (for balance , history and quit , extra words are ignored).

title: 2.01  Methods and Parameters
body: Writing methods with parameters and return values, expression-bodied methods, overloading, optional and named arguments, params arrays, ref, out and in parameters, local functions, recursion, and static methods in classes. Methods A method is a named block of code that takes parameters and may return a value. Methods live in classes; in a top-level program you can also write them directly as local functions : csharp Console.WriteLine(Area(3, 4)); Console.WriteLine(Describe("Ada", 36)); Greet("Grace"); static double Area(double width, double height) { return width height; } static string Describe(string name, int age) = $"{name} ({age})"; // expression-bodied static void Greet(string name) // void: returns nothing { Console.WriteLine($"Hello, {name}!"); } Each parameter has a type, and so does the result: the compiler checks every call. = expression is shorthand for a body that returns one expression. In a class, the same methods look like this; static means they belong to the class itself rather than to an object (lesson 3.05): csharp-norun public static class Geometry { public static double Area(double width, double height) = width height; } // called as Geometry.Area(3, 4) Overloading Several methods in a class may share a name if their parameter lists differ. The compiler picks the best match: csharp Console.WriteLine(MathX.Max(3, 9)); Console.WriteLine(MathX.Max(2.5, 1.5)); Console.WriteLine(MathX.Max(4, 8, 6)); static class MathX { public static int Max(int a, int b) = a b ? a : b; public static double Max(double a, double b) = a b ? a : b; public static int Max(int a, int b, int c) = Max(Max(a, b), c); } Local functions in a top-level program cannot be overloaded; methods in classes can. Optional and named arguments csharp Console.WriteLine(Format(1234.5)); Console.WriteLine(Format(1234.5, decimals: 0)); Console.WriteLine(Format(1234.5, prefix: "EUR ")); static string Format(double amount, int decimals = 2, string prefix = "") = prefix + amount.ToString("F" + decimals); Parameters with default values are optional; they must come after the required ones. Named arguments ( decimals: 0 ) make calls readable and let you skip optional parameters. params A params parameter accepts any number of arguments as an array: csharp Console.WriteLine(Sum()); Console.WriteLine(Sum(1, 2, 3)); int values = { 10, 20 }; Console.WriteLine(Sum(values)); static int Sum(params int numbers) { int total = 0; foreach (int n in numbers) total += n; return total; } ref, out and in Arguments are normally passed by value : the method gets a copy of the variable's value (for reference types, a copy of the reference). Three keywords pass the variable itself: csharp int a = 1, b = 2; Swap(ref a, ref b); Console.WriteLine($"{a} {b}"); if (TryDivide(10, 4, out double result)) Console.WriteLine(result); if (!TryDivide(1, 0, out _)) Console.WriteLine("cannot divide by zero"); static void Swap(ref int x, ref int y) = (x, y) = (y, x); static bool TryDivide(int x, int y, out double quotient) { if (y == 0) { quotient = 0; return false; } quotient = (double)x / y; return true; } - ref : the method can read and change the caller's variable. - out : the method must assign it; used for extra results, as in the TryParse pattern. out _ discards a result you do not need. - in : passed by reference but read-only, to avoid copying large structs. For several results, a tuple is often clearer than out : static (int Min, int Max) Range(int xs) , used as var (lo, hi) = Range(xs); . Recursion A method can call itself. Every recursive method needs a base case that stops: csharp Console.WriteLine(Factorial(10)); Console.WriteLine(Gcd(84, 36)); static long Factorial(int n) = n <= 1 ? 1 : n Factorial(n - 1); static int Gcd(int a, int b) = b == 0 ? a : Gcd(b, a % b); Without a base case, the calls never end and the program stops with a StackOverflowException . Good methods A method should do one thing that its name says. Prefer returning results over printing them: CalculateTotal that returns a number can be tested and reused; one that prints cannot. Keep reading input and printing at the edges of the program.

title: Methods, out parameters and tuples
body: Complete the methods: csharp public static (int Min, int Max, double Mean) Stats(params int values) public static bool TryParseTime(string text, out int minutes) public static string Repeat(string text, int times, string separator = "") public static long Power(long baseValue, int exponent) - Stats throws an ArgumentException when there are no values. - TryParseTime("9:05", out int m) returns true with m = 545 (minutes after midnight). The text must be h:mm or hh:mm with hours 0 to 23 and minutes 00 to 59; otherwise it returns false and sets minutes to 0. - Repeat("ab", 3, "-") is "ab-ab-ab" ; 0 times gives "" . - Power is recursive and fast: b^e is (b^(e/2))² , times b once more when e is odd. e is 0 or more.

title: 2.02  Arrays and Lists
body: Fixed-size arrays and growable List<T - creating, indexing, ranges and Index from the end, iterating, adding, inserting and removing, searching, sorting with comparisons, copying versus sharing, collection expressions, and two-dimensional and jagged arrays. Arrays An array holds a fixed number of values of one type: csharp int scores = new int 3 ; // three zeros scores 0 = 90; scores 2 = 75; string days = { "Mon", "Tue", "Wed" }; int primes = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 ; // a collection expression (C 12) Console.WriteLine(scores.Length); Console.WriteLine(days ^1 ); // last item Console.WriteLine(string.Join(",", primes 1..3 )); // 3,5 Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", scores)); Indexes start at 0. Reading scores 3 throws an IndexOutOfRangeException : C always checks bounds. List<T A List grows and shrinks. List<string is a list of strings: the type in angle brackets is a type argument (generics, lesson 4.01). csharp var names = new List<string { "Grace", "Ada" }; names.Add("Linus"); names.Insert(0, "Ken"); names.Remove("Grace"); // by value; returns false if not found names.RemoveAt(names.Count - 1); // by index Console.WriteLine($"{names.Count}: {string.Join(", ", names)}"); Console.WriteLine(names.Contains("Ada") + " " + names.IndexOf("Ada")); names.AddRange( "Barbara", "Margaret" ); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", names)); Arrays use Length , lists use Count . Use an array when the size is fixed and known; use a list for everything that changes. Iterating csharp List<int numbers = 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42 ; int sum = 0; foreach (int n in numbers) sum += n; for (int i = numbers.Count - 1; i = 0; i--) { if (numbers i % 2 == 1) numbers.RemoveAt(i); // removing: go backwards } Console.WriteLine($"{sum} {string.Join(" ", numbers)}"); Changing a list while foreach walks over it throws InvalidOperationException . Loop backwards with for , or use numbers.RemoveAll(n = n % 2 == 1) . Searching and sorting csharp var words = new List<string { "pear", "fig", "banana", "kiwi" }; words.Sort(); // alphabetical, in place Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", words)); words.Sort((a, b) = a.Length.CompareTo(b.Length)); // by length Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", words)); Console.WriteLine(words.Find(w = w.StartsWith("b"))); Console.WriteLine(words.Exists(w = w.Length 5)); int arr = 5, 1, 4 ; Array.Sort(arr); Console.WriteLine(Array.BinarySearch(arr, 4)); // index 1: needs a sorted array A comparison returns a negative number when a comes first, zero when equal, positive when b comes first; x.CompareTo(y) does that for numbers and strings. List.Sort is not stable: equal items may change order. LINQ's OrderBy (lesson 2.04) is stable and returns a new sequence. Copying versus sharing Arrays and lists are reference types: csharp var a = new List<int { 1, 2 }; var b = a; // the same list var c = new List<int (a); // a copy b.Add(3); Console.WriteLine($"{a.Count} {c.Count}"); // 3 2 int x = 1, 2, 3 ; int y = (int )x.Clone(); y 0 = 9; Console.WriteLine(x 0 ); // 1 A method that receives a list can change the caller's list. If it should not, accept IReadOnlyList<T instead: the method then cannot call Add or Remove . Two dimensions csharp int , grid = new int 3, 4 ; // rectangular: 3 rows, 4 columns grid 1, 2 = 7; Console.WriteLine($"{grid.GetLength(0)}x{grid.GetLength(1)}, {grid 1, 2 }"); int jagged = 1 , 2, 3 , 4, 5, 6 ; // an array of arrays, rows of any length foreach (int row in jagged) Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", row));

title: Arrays and lists
body: Complete the methods. None of them may change the collections they are given. csharp public static int Rotate(int values, int k) // move every item k places to the right, wrapping around public static List<int MergeSorted(IReadOnlyList<int a, IReadOnlyList<int b) public static List<int RunningTotals(IReadOnlyList<int values) // 1, 2, 3 gives 1, 3, 6 public static List<string Compact(IReadOnlyList<string? items) // without nulls, blanks and repeats (first kept), trimmed - Rotate( 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 , 2) is 4, 5, 1, 2, 3 ; a negative k rotates left, and k may be larger than the length. - MergeSorted merges two sorted lists into one sorted list in a single pass (do not just sort the combined list). - Compact compares after trimming: " a", "a", null, " ", "b" gives "a", "b" .

title: 2.03  Dictionaries and Sets
body: Dictionary<TKey, TValue for lookups by key - adding, reading safely with TryGetValue, updating, counting and grouping, iterating key-value pairs - and HashSet<T for unique values and set operations, with case-insensitive keys, sorted variants and queues and stacks. Dictionary A dictionary maps keys to values , with fast lookup by key: csharp var ages = new Dictionary<string, int { "Ada" = 36, "Grace" = 85, }; ages "Linus" = 55; // add or replace ages.Add("Ken", 81); // add; throws if the key exists Console.WriteLine(ages "Ada" ); Console.WriteLine(ages.ContainsKey("Bob")); Console.WriteLine(ages.Count); ages.Remove("Grace"); foreach (var (name, age) in ages) Console.WriteLine($"{name}: {age}"); Reading a missing key with ages "Bob" throws KeyNotFoundException . Read safely with TryGetValue or GetValueOrDefault : csharp var stock = new Dictionary<string, int { "apple" = 3 }; if (stock.TryGetValue("pear", out int pears)) Console.WriteLine(pears); else Console.WriteLine("no pears"); Console.WriteLine(stock.GetValueOrDefault("pear", 0)); Counting and grouping Two patterns that come up constantly: csharp string text = "the cat and the hat and the bat"; var counts = new Dictionary<string, int (); foreach (string word in text.Split(' ')) { counts word = counts.GetValueOrDefault(word) + 1; } Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", counts.Select(kv = $"{kv.Key}={kv.Value}"))); var byFirstLetter = new Dictionary<char, List<string (); foreach (string word in new { "apple", "avocado", "banana", "blueberry", "cherry" }) { if (!byFirstLetter.TryGetValue(word 0 , out var list)) { list = new List<string (); byFirstLetter word 0 = list; } list.Add(word); } foreach (var (letter, words) in byFirstLetter) Console.WriteLine($"{letter}: {string.Join(" ", words)}"); LINQ's GroupBy and CountBy (lesson 2.04) do both in one line, but the loops show what happens. A Dictionary does not promise any order. In practice it keeps insertion order until items are removed, but do not rely on it: sort the keys when the order matters, or use a SortedDictionary , which keeps keys sorted. Keys Keys must not change while in a dictionary, and two keys are the same when Equals says so. For text keys that should ignore case, pass a comparer: csharp var users = new Dictionary<string, string (StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { "Ada" = "admin" }; Console.WriteLine(users "ADA" ); HashSet A HashSet holds unique values with fast Contains : csharp var seen = new HashSet<string (); foreach (string tag in new { "c ", "dotnet", "c ", "linq" }) { if (!seen.Add(tag)) Console.WriteLine($"duplicate: {tag}"); // Add returns false for repeats } var a = new HashSet<int { 1, 2, 3, 4 }; var b = new HashSet<int { 3, 4, 5 }; var both = new HashSet<int (a); both.IntersectWith(b); var either = new HashSet<int (a); either.UnionWith(b); a.ExceptWith(b); Console.WriteLine($"{string.Join(",", both)} {string.Join(",", either)} {string.Join(",", a)}"); list.Contains(x) checks every item; set.Contains(x) takes about the same time however large the set is. When you check membership often, use a set. Queues and stacks csharp var queue = new Queue<string (); // first in, first out queue.Enqueue("first"); queue.Enqueue("second"); Console.WriteLine(queue.Dequeue()); var stack = new Stack<int (); // last in, first out stack.Push(1); stack.Push(2); Console.WriteLine(stack.Pop() + " " + stack.Peek()); Queues suit work waiting its turn (and breadth-first search); stacks suit undo history and matching brackets.

title: Dictionaries and sets
body: Complete the methods: csharp public static Dictionary<string, int WordCounts(string text) // lower-case words; letters and ' only public static List<List<string GroupAnagrams(IEnumerable<string words) public static char? FirstRepeated(string text) // the first character seen a second time public static Dictionary<string, List<string Invert(Dictionary<string, string owners) - WordCounts splits the text into words made of letters and apostrophes (anything else separates words), lower-cased. - GroupAnagrams( "tea", "eat", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat" ) gives "tea", "eat", "ate" , "tan", "nat" , "bat" : groups in the order their first word appears, words in their original order. Anagrams have the same letters in any order; compare ignoring case. - FirstRepeated("swiss") is 's' ; FirstRepeated("abc") is null . - Invert turns item → owner into owner → items, with each owner's items sorted alphabetically (ordinal).

title: 2.04  LINQ
body: Language Integrated Query - filtering, projecting and ordering with Where, Select, OrderBy and ThenBy, aggregates like Count, Sum, Average, Min and Max, First, Any and All, grouping with GroupBy and CountBy, ToDictionary, SelectMany, Distinct, Zip, deferred execution and query syntax. Queries over collections LINQ adds methods to every collection (anything that is an IEnumerable<T ) for filtering, transforming and summarising. Each takes a lambda , a small inline function written x = expression : csharp int numbers = 5, 3, 8, 1, 9, 2 ; var evensSquared = numbers.Where(n = n % 2 == 0).Select(n = n n); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", evensSquared)); // 64 4 Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", numbers.OrderBy(n = n))); Console.WriteLine($"{numbers.Sum()} {numbers.Average():F2} {numbers.Max()} {numbers.Count(n = n 4)}"); using System.Linq; is needed in a project; the practice editor and new projects add it automatically. The common methods Method Gives --- --- Where(x = cond) The items that match Select(x = value) Each item transformed OrderBy(x = key) , OrderByDescending , ThenBy Sorted (stable) First() , FirstOrDefault() , Single() , Last() One item (First throws if none) Any(x = cond) , All(x = cond) , Contains(v) Tests Count() , Sum() , Average() , Min() , Max() Aggregates MinBy(x = key) , MaxBy(x = key) The item with the smallest / largest key Distinct() , DistinctBy(x = key) Without repeats Take(n) , Skip(n) , TakeWhile , Chunk(n) Parts GroupBy(x = key) , CountBy(x = key) Groups / counts per key ToList() , ToArray() , ToDictionary(k, v) , ToHashSet() Collected results SelectMany(x = many) Flattened Zip(other) Pairs Aggregate(seed, (acc, x) = ...) A general fold Working with records LINQ shines on lists of objects. Here, records (lesson 3.02) are short data classes: csharp var people = new List<Person { new("Ada", "London", 36), new("Grace", "New York", 85), new("Linus", "Helsinki", 55), new("Alan", "London", 41), }; var londoners = people.Where(p = p.City == "London").OrderBy(p = p.Name).Select(p = p.Name); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", londoners)); var oldest = people.MaxBy(p = p.Age); Console.WriteLine(oldest!.Name); foreach (var group in people.GroupBy(p = p.City).OrderByDescending(g = g.Count())) { Console.WriteLine($"{group.Key}: {group.Count()} ({string.Join(", ", group.Select(p = p.Name))})"); } var ageByName = people.ToDictionary(p = p.Name, p = p.Age); Console.WriteLine(ageByName "Linus" ); Console.WriteLine(people.Any(p = p.Age 80) + " " + people.All(p = p.Age 30)); record Person(string Name, string City, int Age); GroupBy gives groups, each with a Key and its items. ToDictionary throws if two items have the same key. Flattening and pairing csharp var orders = new { new { "tea", "cake" }, new { "tea" }, new string 0 }; Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", orders.SelectMany(o = o).Distinct())); string names = "Ada", "Grace" ; int scores = 91, 88 ; foreach (var (name, score) in names.Zip(scores)) Console.WriteLine($"{name} {score}"); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", Enumerable.Range(1, 5).Select(i = i i))); Deferred execution Where , Select , OrderBy and most other methods do not run when called: they build a query that runs each time you iterate over it. ToList() , Count() , Sum() and First() run it immediately. csharp var source = new List<int { 1, 2, 3 }; var big = source.Where(n = n 1); // nothing has run yet source.Add(10); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", big)); // 2 3 10: the query sees the new item var snapshot = big.ToList(); // run once and keep the results If you iterate a query several times, or it is expensive, call ToList() once and reuse the list. Query syntax LINQ also has a SQL-like syntax, which the compiler turns into the same method calls: csharp int nums = 4, 9, 1, 7 ; var result = from n in nums where n 3 orderby n descending select n 10; Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", result)); Most C code uses the method syntax; query syntax is sometimes clearer for joins and several from clauses.

title: LINQ queries
body: A shop's sales are records: csharp public record Sale(string Product, string Region, decimal Price, int Quantity); Answer these questions with LINQ (no loops), each as a method in Solution : csharp public static decimal Revenue(IEnumerable<Sale sales) // sum of Price Quantity public static List<string TopProducts(IEnumerable<Sale sales, int n) // by total quantity, ties by name public static Dictionary<string, decimal RevenueByRegion(IEnumerable<Sale sales) public static string? BiggestSale(IEnumerable<Sale sales) // "Product in Region" of the highest Price Quantity, or null public static List<string RegionsSelling(IEnumerable<Sale sales, string product) // distinct regions, sorted

title: 2.05  Nullable Types and Pattern Matching
body: null and nullable reference types, the warnings that catch null bugs, the operators ?. ?? and ??=, nullable value types like int?, tuples, and pattern matching with is, switch expressions, type, relational, logical, property and list patterns. null A reference-type variable can hold null : no object at all. Using a member of null throws NullReferenceException , one of the most common crashes in any program. Modern C projects turn on nullable reference types ( <Nullable enable</Nullable , the default for new projects). Then string means "never null" and string? means "may be null", and the compiler warns when you use a string? without checking: csharp-norun string? middleName = GetMiddleName(); Console.WriteLine(middleName.Length); // warning CS8602: Dereference of a possibly null reference. if (middleName != null) Console.WriteLine(middleName.Length); // fine: checked first Treat these warnings as errors: each one is a possible crash. Null operators csharp string? name = null; Console.WriteLine(name?.Length); // ?. gives null instead of throwing (prints an empty line) int length = name?.Length ?? 0; // ?? supplies a fallback for null Console.WriteLine(length); name ??= "anonymous"; // assign only if null Console.WriteLine(name); string ? tags = null; Console.WriteLine(tags? 0 ?? "no tags"); The ! operator ( name!.Length ) tells the compiler "this is not null"; it changes nothing at run time, so use it only when you are sure. Nullable value types Value types cannot be null, unless you add ? : int? holds an int or null. It suits "no value yet" or "not given": csharp int? score = null; Console.WriteLine(score.HasValue); score = 42; Console.WriteLine(score.Value + 1); int? missing = null; Console.WriteLine((missing ?? -1) + " " + (missing + 5 == null)); // arithmetic with null gives null Tuples A tuple groups a few values without declaring a type, handy for returning several results: csharp var (min, max) = MinMax( 4, 9, 1, 7 ); Console.WriteLine($"{min} {max}"); (string Name, int Age) person = ("Ada", 36); Console.WriteLine(person.Name); static (int Min, int Max) MinMax(int values) = (values.Min(), values.Max()); Pattern matching is tests a value against a pattern , and can capture it in a variable: csharp object things = 42, "hello", 3.5, null!, new List<int { 1, 2 } ; foreach (object thing in things) { if (thing is int n && n 40) Console.WriteLine($"a big int {n}"); else if (thing is string s) Console.WriteLine($"a string of length {s.Length}"); else if (thing is null) Console.WriteLine("null"); else Console.WriteLine($"something else: {thing.GetType().Name}"); } Switch expressions combine patterns into a value: csharp Console.WriteLine(Classify(-5)); Console.WriteLine(Classify(0)); Console.WriteLine(Classify(7)); Console.WriteLine(Classify(150)); Console.WriteLine(Shipping(new Order(30, "NL", false))); Console.WriteLine(Shipping(new Order(120, "NL", false))); Console.WriteLine(Shipping(new Order(10, "US", true))); Console.WriteLine(Describe( 1, 2, 3 ) + " " + Describe( ) + " " + Describe( 7 )); static string Classify(int n) = n switch { < 0 = "negative", 0 = "zero", 0 and <= 100 = "small", _ = "large", }; static decimal Shipping(Order o) = o switch { { Express: true } = 25m, // property pattern { Total: = 100 } = 0m, { Country: "NL" or "BE" } = 4.95m, _ = 12m, }; static string Describe(int xs) = xs switch { = "empty", var only = $"one item {only}", var first, .., var last = $"from {first} to {last}", // list pattern }; record Order(decimal Total, string Country, bool Express); Pattern Matches --- --- 42 , "NL" , null That constant int n , string s That type, captured in a variable < 0 , = 1 and <= 5 Relational, combined with and , or , not { Total: = 100 } Objects whose properties match var a, .., var z Arrays and lists by shape _ Anything (the discard) Arms are tried from top to bottom; the compiler warns when a switch expression does not cover every possible value, and when an arm can never be reached.

title: Pattern matching
body: Complete the methods with switch expressions and patterns: csharp public static string Describe(object? value) public static decimal TicketPrice(int? age, bool student) public static string Summarize(int values) Describe returns: - "nothing" for null - "zero" for the int 0, "negative int" / "positive int" for other ints - "empty text" for "" , otherwise "text of length N" for a string - "list of N" for any List<int - "something else" for anything else TicketPrice (in euros): an unknown age ( null ) pays 12; under 4 pays 0; 4 to 12 pays 6; 65 and over pays 7; students aged 13 to 25 pay 8; everyone else pays 12. Summarize uses list patterns: "none" for an empty array, "just N" for one item, "N and M" for two, and "F ... L (K items)" for more, with the first, last and count.

title: A text report
body: Write a program that reads text until the input ends and prints a report about it. For this input: The cat and the dog. A hedgehog and a cat? No, the dog! it prints: Lines: 4 Words: 13 Distinct words: 7 Longest word: hedgehog Average word length: 3.00 Top words: the 3 a 2 and 2 cat 2 dog 2 Letters: a 6 d 5 e 5 h 5 t 5 Rules: - Words are runs of letters and apostrophes, in lower case (as in practice 2.03): Don't is the word don't . - Lines counts every line read, including empty ones. - Longest word : the longest word; on a tie, the one that appears first. - Average word length has 2 decimals, written with a . (invariant culture). Apostrophes count as characters. - Top words : up to 5 words, most frequent first, ties in alphabetical order (ordinal). Each line is two spaces, the word left-aligned in 12 characters, then the count right-aligned in 3. - Letters : up to 5 of the letters a to z (after lower-casing; other characters are ignored), most frequent first, ties alphabetical. Each line is two spaces, the letter, a space, a bar of , a space and the count. The bar is count 20 / highest count characters (integer division), but at least 1. - With no words at all, print the Lines line and then No words.

title: 3.01  Classes and Properties
body: Defining classes with fields, constructors and methods, properties with get, set, init and validation, auto-properties and required members, primary constructors, access modifiers and encapsulation, object initializers, ToString, and reference semantics. A class A class describes a kind of object: the data each one holds and what it can do. new creates an instance : csharp var acc = new BankAccount("Ada", 100m); acc.Deposit(50m); Console.WriteLine(acc.Withdraw(500m)); // False Console.WriteLine(acc); // calls ToString public class BankAccount { private decimal _balance; // a field: private data public BankAccount(string owner, decimal opening) // the constructor { Owner = owner; Deposit(opening); } public string Owner { get; } // a read-only auto-property public decimal Balance = _balance; // a computed, read-only property public void Deposit(decimal amount) { if (amount < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(amount), "must not be negative"); _balance += amount; } public bool Withdraw(decimal amount) { if (amount _balance) return false; _balance -= amount; return true; } public override string ToString() = $"{Owner}: {_balance:F2}"; } Encapsulation : the balance can only change through Deposit and Withdraw , which keep it valid. Nothing outside the class can set it to -1000. Modifier Visible to --- --- public All code private Only this class (the default for members) protected This class and classes derived from it internal This project (assembly); the default for classes Properties A property looks like a field from outside but runs code. Auto-properties generate the hidden field for you: csharp var p = new Product { Name = "Tea", Price = 2.5m }; p.Price = 3m; Console.WriteLine($"{p.Name} {p.Price} {p.Sku}"); try { p.Price = -1; } catch (ArgumentException e) { Console.WriteLine(e.Message); } public class Product { public required string Name { get; init; } // must be set when created, then fixed public string Sku { get; } = Guid.NewGuid().ToString() ..8 ; // read-only, with an initial value private decimal _price; public decimal Price { get = _price; set { if (value < 0) throw new ArgumentException("price must not be negative"); _price = value; // value is what was assigned } } } Accessors Meaning --- --- { get; set; } Read and write { get; } Set only in the constructor or initializer { get; init; } Set only when the object is created (in an object initializer) { get; private set; } Anyone reads, only the class writes required makes the compiler insist the property is set in the object initializer new Product { Name = ... } . Primary constructors A class can take constructor parameters right after its name. They are in scope in the whole class: csharp var t = new Temperature(21.5); Console.WriteLine($"{t.Celsius} C = {t.Fahrenheit} F"); public class Temperature(double celsius) { public double Celsius = celsius; public double Fahrenheit = celsius 9 / 5 + 32; } Objects are references Variables of a class type hold references . Two variables can point at the same object, and == checks whether they are the same object , not whether they hold equal data: csharp var a = new Point { X = 1, Y = 2 }; var b = a; var c = new Point { X = 1, Y = 2 }; b.X = 10; Console.WriteLine($"{a.X} {a == b} {a == c}"); // 10 True False public class Point { public int X { get; set; } public int Y { get; set; } } For value-based equality, use a record (next lesson). Designing a class - Keep fields private ; expose what callers need through methods and properties. - Check arguments in constructors and setters, so an object can never be in an invalid state. - Make properties read-only ( get / init ) unless something really needs to change them later. - Name classes with nouns ( Invoice ) and methods with verbs ( AddLine ).

title: A playlist class
body: Write a class Playlist that keeps its songs private and valid: csharp var p = new Playlist("Road trip"); p.Add("Africa", 295); // title and length in seconds p.Add("Holiday", 380); p.Name = " Summer "; // trimmed: "Summer" p.Count; // 2 p.TotalSeconds; // 675 p.Duration; // "11:15"; over an hour "1:02:05" p.Remove("holiday"); // true: the first song with that title, ignoring case p.Titles; // a read-only list of titles, in order - Name : a property whose setter trims the value and throws an ArgumentException for an empty or blank name (also in the constructor). - Add throws an ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a length of 0 or less, and an ArgumentException for a blank title. - Duration is m:ss under an hour and h:mm:ss from an hour on. - Titles is an IReadOnlyList<string : changing the playlist afterwards must not change a list you got earlier, and callers cannot add to it.

title: 3.02  Records and Structs
body: Records for data with value equality, positional records, with-expressions for non-destructive changes, deconstruction, record structs; structs as small value types, copying semantics, readonly structs, and choosing between class, record and struct. Records A record is a class meant for data. The compiler generates a constructor, properties, ToString , and value equality : two records are equal when all their properties are equal. csharp var a = new Point(1, 2); var b = new Point(1, 2); Console.WriteLine(a == b); // True: same values Console.WriteLine(a); // Point { X = 1, Y = 2 } var moved = a with { X = 5 }; // a copy with one property changed Console.WriteLine($"{a} {moved}"); var (x, y) = moved; // deconstruction Console.WriteLine(x + y); public record Point(int X, int Y); record Point(int X, int Y) is a positional record : the parameters become init -only properties. Records are immutable by default: instead of changing one, you make a changed copy with with . Records can have methods, extra properties and validation like any class: csharp var order = new Order("A-17", new("tea", 2, 2.5m), new("cake", 1, 4m) ); Console.WriteLine(order.Total); Console.WriteLine(order.Lines 0 ); public record OrderLine(string Item, int Quantity, decimal Price) { public decimal Total = Quantity Price; } public record Order(string Id, List<OrderLine Lines) { public decimal Total = Lines.Sum(l = l.Total); } Value equality compares each property with Equals . A List property compares by reference, so two orders with equal but separate lists are not equal. Use records for data that is compared, copied and passed around: messages, results, settings, keys in dictionaries. Structs A struct is a value type: the variable holds the data itself, and assignment copies it. csharp var p = new Vector2(3, 4); var q = p; // a full copy q.X = 100; Console.WriteLine($"{p.X} {q.X} {p.Length}"); public struct Vector2(double x, double y) { public double X = x; public double Y = y; public readonly double Length = Math.Sqrt(X X + Y Y); } Structs avoid a separate object on the heap, which matters when there are millions of them (points in a game, pixels, money amounts). Built-in examples: int , double , DateTime , TimeSpan , Guid . Guidelines for structs: - Keep them small (a few fields) and immutable : readonly struct , so copies cannot surprise you. - Mutable structs cause bugs: changing a copy (from a list, a property or a method's parameter) does not change the original. csharp var money = new Money(10m, "EUR"); var more = money.Add(new Money(2.5m, "EUR")); Console.WriteLine($"{money} {more} {money == new Money(10m, "EUR")}"); public readonly record struct Money(decimal Amount, string Currency) { public Money Add(Money other) = other.Currency == Currency ? this with { Amount = Amount + other.Amount } : throw new InvalidOperationException("different currencies"); public override string ToString() = $"{Amount:F2} {Currency}"; } A record struct gives a struct the record features: value equality, ToString , with . Choosing Use When --- --- class Objects with identity and behaviour that change over time: an account, a game entity, a service record Data compared by value, usually immutable: a DTO, an event, a result struct / readonly record struct Small values that are copied cheaply: a point, a colour, an amount of money

title: A money value type
body: Write a readonly record struct Money(long Cents, string Currency) . Storing whole cents avoids rounding problems. csharp var price = Money.Parse("12.34 EUR"); // Cents = 1234, Currency = "EUR" var total = price.Add(Money.Parse("0.66 EUR")); total.ToString(); // "13.00 EUR" total.Allocate(3); // 4.34 EUR, 4.33 EUR, 4.33 EUR : the parts add up exactly total == new Money(1300, "EUR"); // true: value equality total with { Currency = "USD" }; // a copy in another currency - Parse reads <amount <currency : the amount has up to 2 decimals and may be negative ( "-5 EUR" , "3.5 USD" ), the currency is 3 capital letters. Anything else throws a FormatException . - Add and Subtract throw an InvalidOperationException when the currencies differ. - ToString writes the amount with 2 decimals and a . : -0.05 EUR . - Allocate(n) splits into n parts that differ by at most one cent, larger parts first, and sum to the original. n must be 1 or more (else ArgumentOutOfRangeException ). Assume the amount is not negative.

title: 3.03  Inheritance and Polymorphism
body: Deriving classes with a base class, calling base constructors, virtual and override, abstract classes and members, sealed, polymorphism through base-class references, protected members, type checks with is and as, and when composition is better than inheritance. Deriving a class A class can inherit from one base class, getting all its members and adding or changing some: csharp Shape shapes = new Circle(1), new Rectangle(2, 3), new Square(2) ; foreach (Shape s in shapes) Console.WriteLine(s.Describe()); Console.WriteLine($"Total area: {shapes.Sum(s = s.Area()):F2}"); public abstract class Shape(string name) { public string Name { get; } = name; public abstract double Area(); // every shape must provide this public virtual string Describe() = $"{Name} with area {Area():F2}"; // may be replaced } public class Circle(double radius) : Shape("circle") { public double Radius { get; } = radius; public override double Area() = Math.PI Radius Radius; } public class Rectangle(double width, double height) : Shape("rectangle") { public double Width { get; } = width; public double Height { get; } = height; public override double Area() = Width Height; } public sealed class Square(double side) : Rectangle(side, side) { public override string Describe() = base.Describe() + " (a square)"; } - : Shape("circle") names the base class and passes arguments to its constructor. - abstract members have no body; an abstract class cannot be created with new and makes derived classes implement them. - virtual members have a default that derived classes may override . In C , methods are not virtual unless you say so. - base.Describe() calls the base class's version. - sealed stops further inheritance. Polymorphism A variable of the base type can hold any derived object. A call to a virtual method runs the version of the actual object: s.Area() runs Circle.Area for a circle. That is polymorphism : code written against Shape works with every shape, including ones written later. Constructors and protected members csharp var e = new Manager("Ada", 5000m, 3); Console.WriteLine($"{e.Name}: {e.MonthlyCost()}"); public class Employee { public string Name { get; } protected decimal Salary { get; } // visible to derived classes, not outside public Employee(string name, decimal salary) { Name = name; Salary = salary; } public virtual decimal MonthlyCost() = Salary; } public class Manager : Employee { private readonly int _reports; public Manager(string name, decimal salary, int reports) : base(name, salary) = _reports = reports; public override decimal MonthlyCost() = base.MonthlyCost() + 200m _reports; } : base(name, salary) runs the base constructor first. The base class sets up its part of the object before the derived class adds its own. Checking types csharp object items = new Circle(2), "text", new Square(1) ; foreach (var item in items) { if (item is Rectangle r) Console.WriteLine($"rectangle {r.Width}x{r.Height}"); else if (item is Shape s) Console.WriteLine($"another shape: {s.Name}"); Shape? maybe = item as Shape; // null if it is not a Shape Console.WriteLine(maybe?.Area().ToString("F1") ?? "not a shape"); } public abstract class Shape(string name) { public string Name { get; } = name; public abstract double Area(); } public class Circle(double r) : Shape("circle") { public override double Area() = Math.PI r r; } public class Rectangle(double w, double h) : Shape("rectangle") { public double Width = w; public double Height = h; public override double Area() = w h; } public class Square(double s) : Rectangle(s, s); If you find yourself writing long chains of is checks to decide what to do, a virtual method on the base class (or a switch expression over a closed set of records) is usually cleaner. Composition over inheritance Inheritance means "is a": a Square is a Rectangle . It ties classes together tightly, and C allows only one base class. When the relationship is "has a" or "uses a", composition (an object holding others) is more flexible: csharp-norun // Inheritance would force: class LoggingRepository : Repository // Composition: the repository is given a logger and uses it. public class OrderService(IOrderRepository repository, ILogger logger) { public void Place(Order order) { repository.Save(order); logger.Log($"placed {order.Id}"); } } Interfaces (next lesson) make composition easy. Keep hierarchies shallow: one or two levels.

title: A payroll with inheritance
body: Build a small class hierarchy: csharp public abstract class Employee(string name) // Name; abstract decimal MonthlyPay(); virtual string Describe() public class Salaried(string name, decimal yearlySalary) : Employee // pay: salary / 12, rounded to cents public class Hourly(string name, decimal rate, double hours) : Employee // pay: rate hours, overtime above 160 hours at 1.5 x rate public class Commissioned(string name, decimal baseSalary, decimal sales, decimal rate) : Salaried // pay: the Salaried pay plus sales rate public static class Payroll { public static decimal Total(IEnumerable<Employee staff) public static string Report(IEnumerable<Employee staff) // one Describe() line per employee, highest pay first } - All pay is rounded to cents with halves away from zero. - Describe() returns "<name : <pay with 2 decimals " by default; Hourly overrides it to add (<hours h) , and Commissioned adds (incl. commission <commission ) , both with invariant formatting. - Report joins the lines with \n ; ties in pay are ordered by name.

title: 3.04  Interfaces
body: Interfaces as contracts, implementing several interfaces, programming against interfaces instead of concrete classes, the built-in IComparable, IEquatable and IEnumerable, default interface methods, explicit implementation, and using interfaces to swap implementations and test code. A contract An interface lists members that a type promises to have, without saying how. A class or struct implements it by providing them all: csharp INotifier channels = new EmailNotifier("ada@example.com"), new SmsNotifier("+3161234") ; foreach (var c in channels) c.Send("Your order has shipped"); Console.WriteLine(channels.Count(c = c.IsAvailable)); public interface INotifier { bool IsAvailable { get; } void Send(string message); } public class EmailNotifier(string address) : INotifier { public bool IsAvailable = address.Contains('@'); public void Send(string message) = Console.WriteLine($"email to {address}: {message}"); } public class SmsNotifier(string number) : INotifier { public bool IsAvailable = number.StartsWith('+'); public void Send(string message) = Console.WriteLine($"sms to {number}: {message ..Math.Min(20, message.Length) }"); } Interface names start with I by convention. A class can inherit from one class but implement any number of interfaces: class Report : Document, IPrintable, IExportable . Program against interfaces Code that takes an interface works with every implementation, including ones that do not exist yet, and including fakes in tests: csharp var clock = new FixedClock(new DateTime(2026, 3, 14, 9, 0, 0)); var greeter = new Greeter(clock); Console.WriteLine(greeter.Greeting("Ada")); public interface IClock { DateTime Now { get; } } public class SystemClock : IClock { public DateTime Now = DateTime.Now; } public class FixedClock(DateTime time) : IClock { public DateTime Now = time; } public class Greeter(IClock clock) { public string Greeting(string name) = clock.Now.Hour switch { < 12 = $"Good morning, {name}", < 18 = $"Good afternoon, {name}", _ = $"Good evening, {name}", }; } Greeter does not care where the time comes from. The real program passes a SystemClock ; a test passes a FixedClock and gets the same answer every time. This is the idea behind dependency injection (lesson 6.03). Accept the most general type you need: a method that only loops over items should take IEnumerable<T , not List<T ; one that needs indexing takes IReadOnlyList<T . Built-in interfaces Interface Lets a type --- --- IComparable<T Be sorted: CompareTo(other) IEquatable<T Compare for equality efficiently: Equals(other) IEnumerable<T Be looped over with foreach and queried with LINQ IDisposable Release resources with using (lesson 4.04) IComparer<T , IEqualityComparer<T Be an external ordering or equality rule csharp var versions = new List<Version3 { new(1, 10, 0), new(1, 2, 3), new(0, 9, 9) }; versions.Sort(); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" < ", versions)); public record Version3(int Major, int Minor, int Patch) : IComparable<Version3 { public int CompareTo(Version3? other) { if (other is null) return 1; int c = Major.CompareTo(other.Major); if (c != 0) return c; c = Minor.CompareTo(other.Minor); return c != 0 ? c : Patch.CompareTo(other.Patch); } public override string ToString() = $"{Major}.{Minor}.{Patch}"; } Default methods and explicit implementation An interface member can have a default implementation , which implementers may keep or replace. It lets you add members to an interface without breaking existing classes: csharp ILogger log = new ConsoleLogger(); log.Info("started"); log.Log("raw message"); public interface ILogger { void Log(string message); void Info(string message) = Log($" info {message}"); // default implementation } public class ConsoleLogger : ILogger { public void Log(string message) = Console.WriteLine(message); } Default members are called through the interface type ( ILogger log ), not through the class. When two interfaces have a member with the same name, or a member should not clutter the class's public surface, implement it explicitly : void IExportable.Export() { ... } . It is then only reachable through the interface. Interfaces or abstract classes? Use an interface to describe a capability that unrelated types can share ( IComparable , INotifier ). Use an abstract base class when types share code and state and form a real "is a" family ( Shape ). Interfaces are the more common choice in modern C .

title: Interfaces for discounts
body: A checkout can apply one discount to an order. Write the interface, three implementations and a chooser: csharp public interface IDiscount { string Name { get; } decimal Apply(decimal total); // the total after the discount, never below 0 } public class PercentOff(decimal percent) : IDiscount // Name "<percent % off", e.g. "10% off" public class AmountOff(decimal amount, decimal minimum) : IDiscount // Name "<amount off over <minimum "; only when total = minimum public class FreeItem(decimal itemPrice) : IDiscount // Name "free item"; the cheapest of nothing: just subtracts itemPrice public static class Checkout { public static (string Name, decimal Total) Best(decimal total, IEnumerable<IDiscount discounts) } - All results are rounded to cents (halves away from zero); amounts in names use invariant formatting without trailing zeros ( 10 , 2.5 ). - Best returns the discount giving the lowest total; on a tie, the one that comes first. With no discount that lowers the total, it returns ("none", total) . Then make orders sortable: a record Order(string Id, int Priority, DateTime Placed) : IComparable<Order that sorts by Priority (1 first), then by Placed (earlier first), then by Id .

title: 3.05  Static Members, Extension Methods and Namespaces
match: 3.05 Static Members, Extension Methods and Namespaces
body: Static fields, properties, methods and constructors, static classes, constants and readonly fields, extension methods that add methods to existing types, namespaces and using directives, file-scoped namespaces, global usings, and organising a project into files. Static members A static member belongs to the class itself, not to any one object. There is exactly one of it: csharp var a = new Ticket(); var b = new Ticket(); Console.WriteLine($"{a.Number} {b.Number} {Ticket.Issued}"); Console.WriteLine(Ticket.Describe(b)); public class Ticket { private static int _next = 1; // shared by all tickets public static int Issued = _next - 1; public int Number { get; } = _next++; // each ticket takes the next number public static string Describe(Ticket t) = $"ticket {t.Number}"; } Static methods cannot use this or instance members, since there is no object. They suit operations that need only their parameters: Math.Max , int.Parse , string.Join , factory methods like Money.FromCents(250) . A static class has only static members and cannot be instantiated: Math , Console , File . Use one for groups of helper functions. Avoid mutable static data where you can: it is shared by the whole program (and every thread), which makes code hard to test. const and readonly csharp Console.WriteLine($"{Limits.MaxUsers} {Limits.StartedAt.Year 2000} {new Circle(2).Area:F2}"); public static class Limits { public const int MaxUsers = 100; // fixed at compile time public static readonly DateTime StartedAt = DateTime.Now; // set once, at run time } public class Circle(double r) { private readonly double _radius = r; // can only be assigned in the declaration or constructor public double Area = Math.PI _radius _radius; } const works for numbers, bool , char and strings known when compiling. readonly fields can hold any value, decided when the program runs, and then never change. Extension methods An extension method adds a method to an existing type without changing it. It is a static method in a static class whose first parameter has this : csharp Console.WriteLine("hello world".Capitalize()); Console.WriteLine("a long sentence that goes on".Truncate(10)); Console.WriteLine(new { 3, 8, 1 }.SecondLargest()); public static class StringExtensions { public static string Capitalize(this string s) = s.Length == 0 ? s : char.ToUpper(s 0 ) + s 1.. ; public static string Truncate(this string s, int max) = s.Length <= max ? s : s ..(max - 1) + "…"; } public static class SequenceExtensions { public static int SecondLargest(this IEnumerable<int values) = values.OrderDescending().Skip(1).First(); } All of LINQ ( Where , Select , ...) is extension methods on IEnumerable<T . They are found when their namespace is imported with using . Namespaces Namespaces group types and keep names from clashing: System.Collections.Generic.List<T . A using directive lets you write the short name: csharp-norun // Models/Invoice.cs namespace Billing.Models; // file-scoped namespace: applies to the whole file public record Invoice(string Id, decimal Total); csharp-norun // Program.cs using Billing.Models; // now Invoice can be used directly using static System.Math; // static members without the class name: Sqrt(2) using Json = System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer; // an alias var invoice = new Invoice("INV-1", 99.5m); Conventions: - The namespace follows the folder: Billing/Models/Invoice.cs holds namespace Billing.Models; . - One public type per file, with the file named after it. - Projects add global usings for common namespaces ( System , System.Linq , System.Collections.Generic ...) with <ImplicitUsings enable</ImplicitUsings , so most files need few using lines. You can add your own in one file: global using Billing.Models; .

title: Extension methods and static state
where: 3.05 Static Members, Extension Methods and Namespaces
body: Write extension methods in a static class TextExtensions : csharp public static bool IsPalindrome(this string text) // ignoring case and anything that is not a letter or digit public static int WordCount(this string text) // runs of non-space characters public static string Abbreviate(this string text, int max) // cut at a word boundary and end with "...", within max characters public static double Median(this IEnumerable<int values) // throws InvalidOperationException when empty and a static class Ids that hands out ids per prefix: csharp Ids.Next("order"); // "order-1" Ids.Next("order"); // "order-2" Ids.Next("user"); // "user-1" Ids.Reset(); // all counters back to the start Abbreviate returns the text unchanged when it fits in max . Otherwise it keeps as many whole words as fit together with "..." (words separated by single spaces in the result) and adds "..." ; if not even the first word fits, it returns just the first max - 3 characters plus "..." .

title: A lending library
body: Model a small lending library with classes, records, inheritance and an interface. Dates are DateOnly values, always passed in, so the code never reads the clock. csharp public record Book(string Isbn, string Title, string Author); public abstract class Member(string id, string name) { public string Id { get; } // as given public string Name { get; } public decimal FinesOwed { get; } // can only be changed by the library (internal or protected setter) public abstract int MaxLoans { get; } public abstract int LoanDays { get; } public virtual decimal FinePerDay = 0.25m; } public class Adult(string id, string name) : Member // 5 loans, 21 days public class Child(string id, string name) : Member // 3 loans, 14 days, 0.10 per day public record Loan(Member Member, Book Book, DateOnly Due); public class Library { public void AddBook(Book book, int copies = 1) public void AddMember(Member member) public Loan Borrow(string memberId, string isbn, DateOnly today) public decimal Return(string memberId, string isbn, DateOnly today) // the fine for this loan public int Available(string isbn) public IReadOnlyList<Loan LoansOf(string memberId) // in the order borrowed public List<string Overdue(DateOnly today) public void PayFine(string memberId, decimal amount) } Rules - AddBook adds copies (adding the same ISBN again adds to its copies); copies must be 1 or more ( ArgumentOutOfRangeException ). AddMember throws an ArgumentException for an id already in use. - Borrow returns the new loan, due LoanDays after today . It throws an InvalidOperationException with exactly one of these messages, checked in this order: unknown member <id , unknown book <isbn , unpaid fines , loan limit reached , already borrowed (the member has this book already), no copies available . - Return throws InvalidOperationException("no such loan") when that member does not have that book. Otherwise it removes the loan and returns the fine: days after the due date × FinePerDay , at most 10.00. The fine is added to the member's FinesOwed . - A member who owes anything cannot borrow until they pay. PayFine lowers FinesOwed by the amount; it throws an ArgumentOutOfRangeException if the amount is 0 or less or more than is owed. - Overdue(today) lists loans with today after the due date as "<name : <title (<days days)" ( 1 day for one), most days first, then by name and title (ordinal).

title: 4.01  Generics
body: Writing type-safe code that works for any type - generic methods and classes, type inference, constraints with where (class, struct, new(), interfaces, notnull), generic interfaces, default(T), covariance in IEnumerable and IReadOnlyList, and why generics beat object. The problem Without generics, a container for "anything" stores object . Every read needs a cast, mistakes show up only when the program runs, and value types get boxed (wrapped in an object) on the way in: csharp-norun var list = new System.Collections.ArrayList(); // the pre-generics collection list.Add(42); list.Add("oops"); // nothing stops this int first = (int)list 0 !; // a cast at every read int second = (int)list 1 !; // InvalidCastException at run time Generics let you write the code once with a type parameter T , and the compiler produces a checked version for every type you use it with: List<int , List<string , Dictionary<string, Order . Generic methods csharp int numbers = 4, 9, 2 ; string words = "pear", "fig" ; Console.WriteLine(Last(numbers)); // T inferred as int Console.WriteLine(Last(words)); // T inferred as string Swap(ref numbers 0 , ref numbers 2 ); Console.WriteLine(string.Join(" ", numbers)); Console.WriteLine(Largest(words) + " " + Largest(numbers)); static T Last<T (IReadOnlyList<T items) = items ^1 ; static void Swap<T (ref T a, ref T b) = (a, b) = (b, a); static T Largest<T (IEnumerable<T items) where T : IComparable<T { using var e = items.GetEnumerator(); if (!e.MoveNext()) throw new InvalidOperationException("empty"); T best = e.Current; while (e.MoveNext()) if (e.Current.CompareTo(best) 0) best = e.Current; return best; } The compiler infers T from the arguments, so you rarely write Last<int (...) .
