title: Searching a folder tree
body: Write the search engine of the file finder (lesson 6.03): wildcard patterns that match like Windows, a recursive walk that skips . , .. and links, depth and size limits, and cancellation through a callback that the UI's stop button controls. The tree is given in memory here; in the real program it comes from FindFirstFileExW (lesson 5.01), and the walk runs on a worker thread (lesson 5.04). cpp struct Entry { std::string name; bool dir{ false }; std::uint64_t size{ 0 }; bool reparse{ false }; // a junction or symbolic link std::vector<Entry children; }; struct Options { std::string patterns; bool recurse{ true }; std::uint64_t minSize{ 0 }; bool includeDirs{ false }; int maxDepth{ -1 }; }; struct Found { std::string path; std::uint64_t size; bool dir; }; bool wildcardMatch(const std::string& pattern, const std::string& name); bool matchesAny(const std::string& patterns, const std::string& name); std::vector<Found search(const Entry& root, const std::string& rootPath, const Options& options, const std::function<bool(int) & keepGoing); wildcardMatch ignores case; matches any run of characters (also none) and ? exactly one. One Windows rule: the pattern . matches every name, with or without a dot. matchesAny takes patterns separated by ; (spaces around them ignored); an empty pattern list matches everything. search walks the tree depth first: - In each directory, entries are visited in name order ignoring case (ties in plain order). Entries called . or .. are skipped entirely. - Each visited entry counts one towards the visit count . A file is found if it matches the patterns and its size is at least minSize ; a directory is found if includeDirs is set and its name matches the patterns. - After each visited entry (found or not), keepGoing(visitCount) is called; if it returns false, the search stops at once and returns what has been found so far. - Then, if the entry is a directory, the search goes into it if recurse is set, it is not a reparse point, and the depth limit allows: the root's entries are at depth 1, and with maxDepth = d , directories at depth d are not entered ( -1 means no limit). - Paths are rootPath + \ + the names on the way down, without doubling a \ that rootPath already ends with.

title: 6.01  Project: A Text Editor
body: Build a complete Notepad-style editor - an edit control or your own text view, files opened and saved in their original encoding and line endings, undo, find and replace, a status bar with line and column, recent files, word wrap and fonts. This lesson is the plan, the key code, and the order to build it in. What you build Xenon Notes - today.md ┌ File Edit Format View Help ─────────────────────────────┐ │ Plans │ │ - finish the editor │ │ - write the finder │ │ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Ln 2, Col 8 100% Windows (CRLF) UTF-8 │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ The in the title means unsaved changes. Every piece comes from an earlier lesson: Piece Lessons --- --- Window, menu, accelerators, recent files 1.03, 2.04, project m02 The text view: an EDIT control, or your own with DirectWrite 2.05, 4.03 Open and Save dialogs with file types 3.02 Reading and writing files safely 5.01 Encodings and line endings 1.02, this lesson's practice Status bar 3.05 Find and Replace dialogs (modeless) 3.01 Settings: font, word wrap, window position 5.02 Drag a file onto the window to open it 5.05 High DPI 3.04 The text view: two options Option 1, the EDIT control. A multi-line EDIT ( ES_MULTILINE ES_AUTOVSCROLL WS_VSCROLL , plus ES_AUTOHSCROLL WS_HSCROLL when word wrap is off) gives you editing, selection, the caret, clipboard and a single undo level for free. Raise its text limit ( EM_SETLIMITTEXT ) above the default 30 000 characters. Word wrap is switched by re-creating the control with or without ES_AUTOHSCROLL , moving the text across. Line and column come from EM_LINEFROMCHAR and EM_LINEINDEX . This is how Notepad was built for decades. Option 2, your own view. A Direct2D window with DirectWrite layouts (lesson 4.03) and your own document model : multi-level undo, syntax colouring, very large files. The project at the end of this milestone writes that model: the text, edits, undo and redo with typing grouped into words, line and column, find and replace. Start with option 1; the model can replace it later without changing the rest of the program. Encodings and line endings A text editor must save a file the way it found it . Opening a file: 1. Read the bytes. 2. Detect the encoding: a BOM (byte order mark) EF BB BF means UTF-8, FF FE UTF-16 little-endian, FE FF UTF-16 big-endian. Without a BOM, check whether the bytes are valid UTF-8 (lesson 1.02's decoder without replacements); if not, assume the legacy code page ( CP_ACP ). 3. Convert to the internal form (UTF-16 for the EDIT control, or UTF-8 for your own model). 4. Detect the line endings: CRLF, LF or CR. If a file mixes them, use the most common one. Remember both, show them in the status bar, and use them when saving: a Unix file with LF endings stays LF, and a UTF-8 file without a BOM stays without one. The practice writes this detection and conversion. Dirty state and closing Track whether the document differs from what is on disk (an EN_CHANGE notification sets the flag; saving clears it), and show it in the title. Every path that discards the document goes through one function: cpp-norun bool confirmDiscard() // true if it is OK to continue { if (!m_dirty) return true; const int answer = MessageBoxW(m_hwnd, (L"Save changes to " + displayName() + L"?").c_str(), L"Xenon Notes", MB_YESNOCANCEL MB_ICONWARNING); if (answer == IDCANCEL) return false; if (answer == IDYES) return save(); // false if the save failed or was cancelled return true; } New, Open, opening a recent file, dropping a file, and WM_CLOSE all call it first. Windows also sends WM_QUERYENDSESSION when the user signs out: answer it the same way. Find and Replace Use modeless dialogs (lesson 3.01) so the user can keep editing. Search from the caret, wrapping around at the end, with "Match case"; Replace All should be one undo step. Keep the last search text so F3 (Find Next) works after the dialog is closed. Order to build in 1. Window, menu and an EDIT control that fills the client area, with the message font. 2. Open and Save As with file dialogs; reading and writing UTF-8. 3. Dirty flag, title, confirmDiscard everywhere. 4. Encoding and line-ending detection, kept when saving; status bar. 5. Find, Find Next, Replace, Go To Line. 6. Word wrap, font selection, zoom; settings saved. 7. Recent files, drag and drop, command-line file argument, high DPI.

title: Opening a file the way it was
match: Opening a file the way it was
body:
Write lesson 6.01's detection and conversion, so the editor saves a file exactly the way it found it: cpp enum class Encoding { Utf8, Utf8Bom, Utf16Le, Utf16Be, Legacy }; enum class LineEnding { Crlf, Lf, Cr }; struct Loaded { std::string text; Encoding encoding; LineEnding ending; }; // text: UTF-8 with 
 line endings Loaded decodeFile(const std::string& bytes); std::string encodeFile(const std::string& text, Encoding encoding, LineEnding ending); bool isValidUtf8(const std::string& bytes); decodeFile - Encoding: EF BB BF at the start is Utf8Bom ; FF FE is Utf16Le ; FE FF is Utf16Be (the BOM is not part of the text). Otherwise valid UTF-8 is Utf8 , and anything else is Legacy , decoded as Latin-1 (each byte is the code point of the same value) for this exercise. - UTF-16 is decoded to UTF-8, including surrogate pairs; an odd final byte is ignored. - Line ending: count 
 , lone  and lone 
 in the decoded text; the most common wins, with ties going to Crlf , then Lf . A text without any line ending is Crlf (the Windows default). - The text is returned with every ending converted to 
 . encodeFile converts 
 to the chosen ending, then writes the encoding with its BOM if it has one ( Legacy writes Latin-1, using ? for characters above U+00FF). isValidUtf8 checks strictly: no overlong forms, no surrogates, nothing above U+10FFFF, no truncated sequence.

title: 6.02  Packaging and Installing
body: Getting a Windows program onto other people's computers - the application manifest, version information, icons, static or dynamic runtime, per-user installs without administrator rights, MSIX and installers, code signing and SmartScreen, and updates. The application manifest The manifest is an XML file embedded in the .exe that tells Windows how to treat the program. Several earlier lessons asked for one; here it is in one place: cpp-norun <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"? <assembly xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v1" manifestVersion="1.0" <assemblyIdentity type="win32" name="Xenon.Notes" version="1.2.0.0"/ <dependency <dependentAssembly <!-- lesson 3.05: visual styles -- <assemblyIdentity type="win32" name="Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls" version="6.0.0.0" processorArchitecture=" " publicKeyToken="6595b64144ccf1df" language=" "/ </dependentAssembly </dependency <trustInfo xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v3" <security <requestedPrivileges <requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker" uiAccess="false"/ <!-- no administrator prompt -- </requestedPrivileges </security </trustInfo <application xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v3" <windowsSettings <dpiAwareness xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/SMI/2016/WindowsSettings" PerMonitorV2</dpiAwareness <!-- 3.04 -- <longPathAware xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/SMI/2016/WindowsSettings" true</longPathAware <!-- 5.01 -- <activeCodePage xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/SMI/2019/WindowsSettings" UTF-8</activeCodePage <!-- 1.02 -- </windowsSettings </application </assembly Add it in Visual Studio under Manifest Tool Input and Output Additional Manifest Files . asInvoker is right for almost every program: requesting requireAdministrator makes every start show a UAC prompt, which users rightly distrust. Version information and icon A VERSIONINFO resource (lesson 2.04) puts the version, product name, company and copyright in the file's Properties dialog. The version is four 16-bit numbers, major.minor.patch.build , stored as two 32-bit values ( FILEVERSION 1,2,0,0 ). The practice packs, unpacks and compares them, which is also what an update check does. The icon resource with the lowest id becomes the .exe 's icon in Explorer; include all sizes (lesson 3.04). Runtime and dependencies - Link the C runtime statically ( /MT ) to avoid requiring the Visual C++ Redistributable, or install the redistributable with your installer if you link dynamically ( /MD ). - Ship any DLLs you use next to the .exe (the DLL course explains the search order). - Test on a clean Windows virtual machine or Windows Sandbox: the only reliable way to find a missing dependency. Installing per user A program does not need administrator rights to be installed. A per-user install puts it in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<Name and writes only to HKEY_CURRENT_USER : What Where --- --- Program files %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\XenonNotes\ Start menu shortcut %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\ File associations HKCU\Software\Classes (lesson 5.05) Entry in Settings Apps HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\XenonNotes with DisplayName , DisplayVersion , Publisher , UninstallString Per-machine installs into Program Files need administrator rights once, during installation. Installer options Tool Notes --- --- MSIX Windows' modern package format: clean install and uninstall, automatic updates, required for the Microsoft Store; must be signed WiX Toolset Builds MSI installers from XML; the standard for enterprise deployment Inno Setup , NSIS Script-based .exe installers, simple and popular for small programs A zip For tools that need no installation at all ("portable") Whatever you use, uninstalling must remove everything the installer added, and nothing the user created. Code signing and SmartScreen An unsigned downloaded .exe shows SmartScreen 's "Windows protected your PC" warning. Signing with a code-signing certificate ( signtool sign /fd SHA256 /tr <timestamp server /td SHA256 app.exe ) identifies you as the publisher; the warning disappears as the signature builds reputation. Always add a timestamp so the signature stays valid after the certificate expires. Microsoft's Trusted Signing service and the Microsoft Store are alternatives to buying a certificate. Updates The simplest update check downloads a small file with the latest version number (over HTTPS, with WinHTTP or URLDownloadToFileW ), compares it with the running version, and offers a download page. Never run downloaded code without verifying its signature. MSIX and the Store handle updates themselves.

title: Version numbers
body: Windows stores a file version as four 16-bit numbers in two 32-bit values ( VS_FIXEDFILEINFO 's dwFileVersionMS and dwFileVersionLS ). Write the helpers an about box and an update check need: cpp struct Version { std::uint16_t major{ 0 }, minor{ 0 }, patch{ 0 }, build{ 0 }; }; bool parseVersion(const std::string& text, Version& out); std::string formatVersion(const Version& v, int parts); // 1 to 4 parts, e.g. formatVersion(v, 3) == "1.2.0" void packVersion(const Version& v, std::uint32_t& ms, std::uint32_t& ls); Version unpackVersion(std::uint32_t ms, std::uint32_t ls); int compareVersions(const Version& a, const Version& b); // -1, 0 or 1 bool updateAvailable(const std::string& running, const std::string& latest); - parseVersion accepts 1 to 4 numbers separated by dots, each 0 to 65535, optionally starting with v or V ; missing parts are 0. Anything else (empty parts, letters, a fifth part, spaces) fails. - packVersion : ms = major << 16 minor , ls = patch << 16 build . - updateAvailable is true only if both strings parse and latest is newer.

title: 6.03  Project: A File Finder
body: Build a fast file search tool - a search box with options, a worker thread walking folders, results streaming into a virtual list view, sorting, progress and cancellation, opening results and showing them in Explorer. This lesson ties milestones 3 and 5 together. What you build Xenon Finder ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Look in C:\Users\Sam\Documents Browse... │ │ Names .md; .txt x Subfolders Search │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Name ▲ Folder Size Modified │ │ notes.md C:\...\Projects 2.4 KB 2026-11-02 │ │ plan.txt C:\...\Xenon 812 b 2026-10-18 │ │ ... │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Searching C:\Users\Sam\Documents\Archive... 1 204 found │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ The pieces Piece From --- --- Layout that resizes, at any DPI 3.03, 3.04 Folder picker 3.02 ( FOS_PICKFOLDERS ) Wildcards, recursion, skipping links, cancellation project m05 Worker thread and posting results 5.04 Virtual list: sorting, selection, status text 3.05, project m03 Opening a result, "show in folder" 5.03 Copying paths to the clipboard 5.05 Settings: last folder, patterns, column widths 5.02 Threading the search The search runs on a worker; the UI thread only displays. The tricky part is how results travel: - Posting a message per file floods the queue with tens of thousands of messages and the UI stutters. - Collect results in a vector protected by a lock (or a work queue, practice 5.04), and post one "new results" message at most every 100 ms. The UI thread swaps the batch out, appends it to the list's model, and calls ListView_SetItemCountEx once. - The status bar shows the folder currently being searched, also throttled. The practice writes the throttle. cpp-norun case WM_APP_RESULTS: { std::vector<Item batch; { std::lock_guard lock{ m_shared.mutex }; batch.swap(m_shared.pending); m_shared.posted = false; } m_model.append(std::move(batch)); // project m03's ResultList, extended with append ListView_SetItemCountEx(m_list, m_model.count(), LVSICF_NOINVALIDATEALL LVSICF_NOSCROLL); updateStatus(); return 0; } A new search, closing the window, or the Stop button sets the stop flag and joins the old worker before anything else (with std::jthread , assigning a new thread does this). Never let two searches write into the same results. Sorting while results arrive Sorting a list that keeps growing must not make rows jump under the user's mouse. A simple rule: while searching, append in arrival order; when the search finishes (or the user clicks a column), sort once. Selection is kept by id (project m03), so it survives. Actions on results - Enter or double-click: open with the default program ( ShellExecuteExW , lesson 5.03). - Ctrl+Enter or the context menu's "Show in folder": SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems , or explorer.exe /select,"path" (quoted with practice 5.03's rules). - Ctrl+C : copy the selected paths, one per line with CRLF (lesson 5.05). - Delete : move to the Recycle Bin with IFileOperation ( FOFX_RECYCLEONDELETE ), never a permanent delete, and remove the rows. Speed FindFirstFileExW with FindExInfoBasic (no short 8.3 names) and FIND_FIRST_EX_LARGE_FETCH is noticeably faster than plain FindFirstFileW . Skipping folders you cannot open (error 5) silently, rather than reporting each one, keeps the search going through protected system folders. For whole-drive searches, real tools read the NTFS change journal or the Windows Search index; walking folders is fast enough for a few hundred thousand files. Order to build in 1. Window with the controls and layout; the folder picker. 2. A search on the UI thread into a plain list: correct results first. 3. Move it to a worker; post batches; Stop button. 4. Virtual list view with the model from project m03; sorting and status text. 5. Actions: open, show in folder, copy, delete to the Recycle Bin. 6. Settings, high DPI, keyboard navigation everywhere.

title: Batching results for the UI
body: Write the two pieces between lesson 6.03's worker thread and its window: a throttle that decides when to post, and a batch that collects results in between. Time is given in milliseconds by the caller so the logic can be tested: cpp class Throttle { public: explicit Throttle(int intervalMs); bool ready(long long nowMs); // true at most once per interval; the first call is always ready bool finish(); // true if anything was held back since the last time ready() was true void held(); // something happened that was not reported yet }; template <typename T class Batch { public: bool add(T item); // true if the window must be told (no message is pending) std::vector<T take(); // the UI thread takes everything; the next add() will ask again std::size_t pending() const; }; Throttle : ready(now) returns true if this is the first call, or at least intervalMs have passed since the last time it returned true; then it also forgets anything held. held() marks that something was not reported; finish() returns whether such a thing is still unreported (and clears it), so the final state is always shown when the search ends. Batch (used from two threads, so protect it with a mutex): add appends the item and returns true only if no "new results" message is pending yet, and then marks one as pending; take returns all items, clears the batch and the pending mark. So however many items arrive, at most one message is in the queue.

title: The text editor's document
body:
Write the document model behind lesson 6.01's editor: the text, edits, multi-level undo and redo with typing grouped into words, the unsaved-changes flag, line and column, find, and Replace All as a single undo step. A text view (an EDIT control replacement drawn with DirectWrite, lesson 4.03) then only displays it and turns keys into calls. cpp struct LineCol { int line, col; }; // both 1-based class TextDocument { public: explicit TextDocument(std::string text = ""); const std::string& text() const; void insert(std::size_t pos, const std::string& s); void erase(std::size_t pos, std::size_t count); void replace(std::size_t pos, std::size_t count, const std::string& s); void breakGroup(); bool undo(); bool redo(); bool modified() const; void markSaved(); LineCol lineCol(std::size_t pos) const; std::size_t offsetOf(int line, int col) const; std::optional<std::size_t find(const std::string& what, std::size_t from, bool matchCase, bool wrap) const; int replaceAll(const std::string& what, const std::string& with, bool matchCase); }; Edits and undo : positions beyond the end are clamped to the end (and counts to what is there). Every edit that changes something becomes an undo step and clears the redo list. replace is one step. undo reverts the last step and redo re-applies it; both return false when there is nothing to do. Typing groups : an insert of a single character joins the previous step instead of making a new one when: - the previous step was also made by insert and nothing has broken the group since ( breakGroup , undo , redo , markSaved or any other kind of edit break it), - it continues exactly where the previous step's text ended, - the character is not 
 , and the previous step does not end with a space unless this character is a space too (so a word and the spaces after it form one step). Modified is true when the text differs from the last saved (or initial) state as far as undo can tell: track the position in the undo history. lineCol counts lines from 1, starting after each 
 , and columns from 1 (in bytes). offsetOf clamps the line to the existing lines and the column to 1 .. length of the line + 1 (the line's length excludes its 
 ). find searches forward from from , ignoring case unless matchCase ; with wrap , if nothing is found from from , it searches again from the start. An empty what finds nothing. replaceAll replaces every non-overlapping match from left to right, as one undo step, and returns how many it replaced (0 changes nothing and adds no step).

title: Cheat Sheet - Win32
body: The skeleton cpp-norun define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN define NOMINMAX include <windows.h LRESULT CALLBACK WndProc(HWND hwnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam) { switch (msg) { case WM_CREATE: / create controls / return 0; case WM_SIZE: / layout(LOWORD(lParam), HIWORD(lParam)) / return 0; case WM_PAINT: { PAINTSTRUCT ps; HDC dc = BeginPaint(hwnd, &ps); / draw / EndPaint(hwnd, &ps); return 0; } case WM_CLOSE: / ask to save; then / DestroyWindow(hwnd); return 0; case WM_DESTROY: PostQuitMessage(0); return 0; } return DefWindowProcW(hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam); } int WINAPI wWinMain(HINSTANCE inst, HINSTANCE, PWSTR, int show) { WNDCLASSEXW wc{ sizeof(wc) }; wc.lpfnWndProc = WndProc; wc.hInstance = inst; wc.lpszClassName = L"Main"; wc.hCursor = LoadCursorW(nullptr, IDC_ARROW); wc.hbrBackground = reinterpret_cast<HBRUSH (COLOR_WINDOW + 1); RegisterClassExW(&wc); HWND hwnd = CreateWindowExW(0, L"Main", L"Title", WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW, CW_USEDEFAULT, CW_USEDEFAULT, 800, 500, nullptr, nullptr, inst, nullptr); ShowWindow(hwnd, show); MSG m; while (GetMessageW(&m, nullptr, 0, 0) 0) { TranslateMessage(&m); DispatchMessageW(&m); } return static_cast<int (m.wParam); } Messages Message wParam / lParam --- --- WM_SIZE type / LOWORD width, HIWORD height WM_LBUTTONDOWN , WM_MOUSEMOVE MK_ flags / GET_X_LPARAM , GET_Y_LPARAM (signed) WM_MOUSEWHEEL GET_WHEEL_DELTA_WPARAM (120 per notch) / screen position WM_KEYDOWN , WM_KEYUP virtual key / repeat count, scan code, bit 30 = was down WM_CHAR UTF-16 unit / as for keys WM_COMMAND LOWORD id, HIWORD code (0 menu, 1 accelerator, else notification) / control WM_NOTIFY id / NMHDR WM_TIMER timer id / callback WM_DPICHANGED HIWORD new DPI / suggested RECT WM_APP + n your own messages PostMessageW queues and returns; SendMessageW calls and waits. Errors Code Meaning --- --- 2 / 3 File / path not found 5 Access denied 32 Sharing violation (file in use) 87 Invalid parameter 183 Already exists 1223 Cancelled by the user FAILED(hr) for HRESULTs; HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(code) ; FormatMessageW for text. Strings cpp-norun MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, MB_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf8, len, nullptr, 0); // size first, then convert WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, WC_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf16, len, nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr); Controls Task Call --- --- Find a control GetDlgItem(parent, id) Text SetDlgItemTextW , GetDlgItemTextW , GetWindowTextLengthW Check box CheckDlgButton , IsDlgButtonChecked List box LB_ADDSTRING , LB_GETCURSEL , LB_FINDSTRING Font SendMessageW(ctrl, WM_SETFONT, (WPARAM)font, TRUE) Tab navigation IsDialogMessageW in the loop Move many BeginDeferWindowPos / DeferWindowPos / EndDeferWindowPos Drawing GDI Direct2D --- --- BeginPaint / EndPaint BeginDraw / EndDraw (check D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET ) CreatePen , CreateSolidBrush + SelectObject + DeleteObject CreateSolidColorBrush (a ComPtr) FillRect , Rectangle , Ellipse , LineTo FillRectangle , DrawRectangle , FillEllipse , DrawLine DrawTextW DrawTextLayout with a DirectWrite layout InvalidateRect(hwnd, &r, FALSE) the same RGB(r, g, b) = 0x00BBGGRR D2D1::ColorF(r, g, b, a) with floats 0..1 DPI cpp-norun const UINT dpi = GetDpiForWindow(hwnd); int px = MulDiv(designPx, dpi, 96); int fontHeight = -MulDiv(points, dpi, 72); Files and system Task Call --- --- Open a file CreateFileW(path, GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ, nullptr, OPEN_EXISTING, 0, nullptr) List a folder FindFirstFileExW / FindNextFileW / FindClose (skip . , .. , reparse points) Replace safely write a temp file, then ReplaceFileW or MoveFileExW(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING) Settings folder SHGetKnownFolderPath(FOLDERID_RoamingAppData, ...) Registry RegGetValueW , RegCreateKeyExW , RegSetValueExW (size in bytes incl. null) Run a program CreateProcessW(nullptr, mutableCmdLine, ...) , close both handles Open a document ShellExecuteExW with verb open Worker to UI PostMessageW(hwnd, WM_APP + n, 0, (LPARAM)new Data) Clipboard OpenClipboard , EmptyClipboard , SetClipboardData(CF_UNICODETEXT, hglobal) , CloseClipboard Dropped files DragAcceptFiles , WM_DROPFILES , DragQueryFileW , DragFinish

title: Common Errors
body: Message or symptom Usual cause Fix Lesson --- --- --- --- Errors about min or max in standard headers windows.h defines min and max macros define NOMINMAX before including it 1.01 Text shows as ? or boxes The A functions with a legacy code page, or UTF-8 passed where UTF-16 is expected Call the W functions; convert at the boundary 1.02 The window cannot be moved, resized or closed Unhandled messages not passed to DefWindowProcW Return DefWindowProcW(...) for everything you do not handle 1.03 The program keeps running after the window closes No PostQuitMessage in WM_DESTROY Call PostQuitMessage(0) 1.03 One CPU core at 100 % WM_PAINT without BeginPaint / EndPaint , so the area never becomes valid Always pair them 1.05 Drawing stops after a while GDI objects leaked (deleted while selected, or never deleted) Select the old object back, then DeleteObject ; watch "GDI objects" in Task Manager 1.05 Mouse positions jump to about 65 000 LOWORD used for coordinates on multi-monitor setups GET_X_LPARAM / GET_Y_LPARAM 1.04 Typed text has the wrong letters on some keyboards Text built from WM_KEYDOWN Use WM_CHAR (and keep TranslateMessage in the loop) 2.01 Alt+F4 stops working WM_SYSKEYDOWN swallowed Pass system keys you do not use to DefWindowProcW 2.01 A drag gets stuck "pressed" Capture lost without a button-up Handle WM_CAPTURECHANGED 2.02 A countdown runs slow Counting WM_TIMER ticks Compute from the real clock 2.03 Ctrl+S does nothing although the menu shows it No accelerator table, or TranslateAcceleratorW missing from the loop Load the table and translate before dispatching 2.04 Controls look like Windows 95 No common controls v6 manifest entry Add the dependency (lesson 3.05) 3.05 Controls use a bold old font Controls not given a font WM_SETFONT with the message font 2.05 Tab does nothing No IsDialogMessageW in the loop Add it, and WS_TABSTOP on controls 2.05 The program is blurry on a laptop Not DPI aware Per-monitor v2 in the manifest; scale sizes 3.04 Everything is tiny at 150 % DPI aware but sizes not scaled MulDiv(value, dpi, 96) everywhere 3.04 Flicker when resizing Background erased before painting Return 1 from WM_ERASEBKGND ; double buffer; WS_CLIPCHILDREN 4.01 The window goes blank after a driver update Direct2D device loss ignored Re-create device resources on D2DERR_RECREATE_TARGET 4.02 Edges of transparent images have dark fringes Straight alpha filtered as premultiplied Convert to 32bppPBGRA 4.04 "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process" (32) Share mode conflict Use suitable share modes; retry briefly 5.01 A recursive search never ends . , .. or links followed Skip them and reparse points 5.01 A registry string is cut in half Size passed in characters instead of bytes (length + 1) sizeof(wchar_t) 5.02 Access denied writing settings Writing to HKLM or Program Files Use HKCU and AppData 5.02 CreateProcessW crashes A string literal passed as the command line Pass a writable buffer 5.03 Arguments with spaces break Missing or wrong quoting Quote with the backslash rules 5.03 Reading a child's output hangs Our copy of the pipe's write end still open Close it after CreateProcessW 5.03 The window freezes ("Not responding") Long work or waiting on the UI thread Move it to a worker thread 5.04 Random crashes with threads Data shared without a lock, or a worker touching windows Lock shared data; post messages to the UI thread 5.04 A deadlock between two threads SendMessageW to a waiting thread, or locks taken in different orders PostMessageW ; one lock order 5.04 Pasted text has odd line breaks Line endings not normalised Convert \r\n , \r and \n 5.05 SmartScreen warns about the program The .exe is not signed Code-sign with a timestamp 6.02

title: Glossary
body: Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets. Term Meaning --- --- Accelerator table A table mapping key combinations to command ids, translated in the message loop. (2.04) Anchor Which edges of its parent a control keeps a fixed distance from when the parent is resized. (3.03) BOM Byte order mark: bytes at the start of a text file that identify its encoding ( EF BB BF , FF FE , FE FF ). (6.01) Capture Directing all mouse messages to one window, even when the mouse is outside it. (2.02) Client area The inside of a window, without the frame, title bar and menu. (1.03) COM Windows' component object model: objects created by class id, used through interfaces, released when done. (3.02) Common controls List view, tree view, status bar and other controls from comctl32, drawn with visual styles in version 6. (3.05) Device context (HDC) A drawing surface with its current pen, brush, font and colours. (1.05) Device-dependent resource A Direct2D object on the GPU that must be re-created when the device is lost. (4.02) Dialog unit The layout unit of dialog templates, based on the dialog's font, so dialogs scale with text size. (3.01) DIP Device-independent pixel: 1/96 inch, Direct2D's unit when DPI is set. (4.02) Direct2D The GPU-accelerated 2D drawing API with antialiasing and transforms. (4.02) DirectWrite The text layout and rendering API used with Direct2D. (4.03) Double buffering Drawing a frame off-screen and copying it to the window in one step, to avoid flicker. (4.01) DPI awareness A program's declaration that it scales itself for the monitor's DPI instead of being stretched. (3.04) GDI The original Windows drawing API: device contexts, pens, brushes, fonts, bitmaps. (1.05) GetLastError Returns the thread's last error code, set by most failing API functions. (1.01) Handle An opaque value referring to a system object, closed with its type's own function. (1.01) HRESULT A 32-bit result code used by COM: negative means failure. (1.01) Invalid region The part of a window that needs repainting; WM_PAINT is sent while it is not empty. (1.05) Known folder A standard folder such as AppData or Documents, located with SHGetKnownFolderPath. (5.01) Manifest XML embedded in an .exe that sets visual styles, DPI awareness, privileges and more. (6.02) Message A notification (input, painting, timers, commands) delivered to a window procedure. (1.03) Message loop The loop that takes messages from the thread's queue and dispatches them. (1.03) Modal / modeless A dialog that blocks its owner until closed, or one that stays open alongside it. (3.01) Notification A control's message to its parent about an event: WM_COMMAND codes or WM_NOTIFY structures. (2.05, 3.05) Posted / sent message A message put in the queue and returned from at once, or delivered directly with the caller waiting. (1.04) Premultiplied alpha Pixels whose colour channels are already multiplied by their alpha. (4.04) Registry Windows' hierarchical database of keys and typed values. (5.02) Reparse point A junction or symbolic link in the file system, which can point anywhere, including back up the tree. (5.01) Resource Data compiled into the .exe: menus, dialogs, icons, strings, version information. (2.04) Share mode What other programs may do with a file while you have it open. (5.01) Surrogate pair Two UTF-16 code units encoding one code point above U+FFFF. (1.02) Text layout A DirectWrite object holding one string laid out in a box, for drawing and hit-testing. (4.03) UI thread The thread that owns the windows and runs the message loop; it must never block. (5.04) UTF-16 The encoding Windows uses internally: 16-bit units, with surrogate pairs for rare characters. (1.02) Virtual list view A list view that stores no items and asks for the text of visible rows only. (3.05) Virtual-key code The number identifying a physical key in key messages, such as VK_LEFT or 'A'. (2.01) Visual styles The modern look of controls, enabled by the common controls version 6 manifest entry. (3.05) W and A functions The UTF-16 (wide) and legacy code page (ANSI) versions of text functions. (1.02) WIC The Windows Imaging Component, which decodes and encodes image files. (4.04) Window class A registered description of a kind of window, including its window procedure. (1.03) Window procedure The function that handles a window's messages. (1.03) Worker thread A thread that does slow work and posts results to the UI thread. (5.04)
